classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: xenon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate for xenon atoms supplied by gas injection, assigning 54 equivalent electrons to each xenon atom.
items.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which xenon is supplied by gas injection, expressed on an equivalent-electron basis. It represents injected xenon inventory rather than electron production or the xenon content already present in the plasma. The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t) = 54\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t) $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate, $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the atomic number of xenon, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Xe}}(t)$ is the xenon-atom injection rate due to gas injection, and $t$ is time. The quantity applies only to xenon supplied by gas injection and aggregates the injected xenon-atom rate by weighting each atom with xenon's atomic number. It is species-resolved and instantaneous, not a total rate over all injected gasses. The factor 54 is an equivalent-electron bookkeeping convention based on nuclear charge, not a count of free electrons produced by ionization. This rate is distinct from an accumulated xenon inventory; integrating it over time gives the equivalent-electron inventory delivered by gas injection. The same species-resolved convention is used for the [helium-4 gas-injection source rate](name:helium_4_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) and [hydrogen gas-injection source rate](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection).

items.name: parallel_wave_electric_field_real_part
items.description: Signed in-phase quadrature of the coherent wave electric-field phasor projected along the local equilibrium magnetic field, relative to the chosen wave phase reference.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed in-phase quadrature of the wave electric-field phasor parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It describes local wave polarization along a beam or ray path relative to a chosen phase reference. The defining projection and real-part operation are $$ E_{\parallel,\mathrm{R}} = \operatorname{Re}\widetilde E_\parallel = \operatorname{Re}\left(\widetilde{\mathbf E}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right) $$ where $E_{\parallel,\mathrm{R}}$ is this real quadrature, $\widetilde E_\parallel$ is the [parallel wave electric-field phasor](name:parallel_wave_electric_field), $\widetilde{\mathbf E}$ is the full wave electric-field phasor, and $\hat{\mathbf b}$ is the unit vector along the local equilibrium magnetic field. Together with the [imaginary quadrature](name:parallel_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part), denoted $E_{\parallel,\mathrm{I}}$, it reconstructs the parent phasor through $\widetilde E_\parallel=E_{\parallel,\mathrm{R}}+iE_{\parallel,\mathrm{I}}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit. Its value depends on the phase reference; it is neither the phasor magnitude nor the instantaneous oscillating field. The quantity is local along the propagation path, not a path integral or average, and excludes the equilibrium electric field. Unlike the [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric-field real part](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part), it resolves the field-aligned component rather than a transverse circular polarization component. Sign convention: Positive when the in-phase wave electric-field projection points along the local equilibrium magnetic field at the chosen phase reference.

items.name: ion_fluence_at_divertor_target
items.description: Cumulative incident ion-particle dose delivered to a divertor target, with each ion counted once across all species and charge states.
items.documentation: Ion fluence at a divertor target is the cumulative number of incident ions per unit target area over a specified time interval. It is the ion-only component of fluence at the divertor target, including all ionic species and charge states while counting each incident ion once. $$ \Phi_{\mathrm{ion}} = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} \left[\sum_{s\in\mathcal{I}} \Gamma_{\perp,s}(t)\right] \, dt $$ Here, $\Phi_{\mathrm{ion}}$ is the ion fluence, $t_1$ and $t_2$ are the interval endpoints in seconds, $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of included ion species and charge states, and $\Gamma_{\perp,s}$ is the incident normal particle-flux density for state $s$, in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. The flux is directed from the plasma toward the target surface. Neutral atoms, molecules, and nonparticle channels are excluded.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity
items.description: Radial component of the complex first-order plasma velocity perturbation eigenfunction for a specified toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis, abstracting over its real and imaginary scalar parts.
items.documentation: The radial perturbed plasma velocity is the radial projection of the full complex eigenfunction of [perturbed_plasma_velocity](name:perturbed_plasma_velocity), characterizing the component of first-order oscillatory plasma flow directed along the major-radius coordinate $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. This component is central to stability analyzes of interchange, ballooning, and peeling modes, where cross-field plasma displacement drives the instability. The physical time-domain radial perturbation is recovered as: $$ \delta v_r(\mathbf{r}, t) = \mathrm{Re}\!\left[\delta\hat{v}_r(\mathbf{r})\, e^{-i\omega t}\right] $$ where $\omega$ is the complex mode eigenfrequency and $\delta\hat{v}_r(\mathbf{r})$ is the complex scalar radial eigenfunction amplitude. As a complex phasor, it decomposes into the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part) $\mathrm{Re}(\delta\hat{v}_r)$, the in-phase fluid-velocity amplitude, and the [imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part) $\mathrm{Im}(\delta\hat{v}_r)$, the quadrature component relative to the chosen eigenmode phase normalization. The radial plasma displacement eigenfunction is related by $\xi_r = \delta\hat{v}_r / (-i\omega)$, linking fluid velocity to flux-surface deformation. This eigenfunction component is evaluated by linear MHD eigenvalue solvers as part of the full toroidal Fourier harmonic decomposition of the perturbed velocity field. It contributes to the per_toroidal_mode_perturbed_energy alongside poloidal and toroidal velocity components, and couples to eigenfunction components such as [perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part](name:perturbed_plasma_pressure_real_part) through the linearized momentum equation. Sign convention: Positive when the radial fluid motion is directed in the direction of increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local helium-4 ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states.
items.documentation: Particle number density of the helium-4 ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local helium-4 ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states. It represents helium-4 ions specifically, rather than neutral helium, electrons, other isotopes, or another plasma population. The defining relation is $$ n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ion}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density at the magnetic axis, $N_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ion}}$ is the number of helium-4 ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume. The superscript $4$ identifies the helium isotope with four nucleons. The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete helium-4 ion population at that location and is summed over all helium-4 ionic charge states; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density of neutral helium or another isotope. This is the helium-4-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis), whose population is left unspecified at the parent level. It is distinguished from [helium-3 density at the magnetic axis](name:helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis), which counts helium-3 ions rather than helium-4 ions.

items.name: vertical_wave_vector_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description: Signed vertical component of the electromagnetic wave vector along a beam-tracing beam, giving local spatial phase variation with vertical height.
items.documentation: The vertical wave-vector component is the signed projection of the local electromagnetic wave vector onto the vertical direction, evaluated locally along a beam-tracing beam. The component is defined by $$ k_Z = \mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} = \frac{\partial S}{\partial Z}. $$ Here $k_Z$ is the vertical wave-vector component, $\mathbf{k}$ is the local [wave vector](name:wave_vector), and $S$ is the wave phase whose spatial gradient is $\mathbf{k}$. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ points along the positive toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the [vertical coordinate of the beam position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_beam). This quantity applies pointwise along the beam path and is not restricted to the launch point; no path integration or averaging is implied. It retains the spatial phase scale, unlike the [normalized vertical wave-vector component](name:vertical_wave_vector_normalized_of_beam_tracing_beam), which equals $k_Z/|\mathbf{k}|$ for a nonzero wave vector, where $|\mathbf{k}|$ is the wave-vector magnitude. Sign convention: Positive when the wave vector has a component toward increasing vertical coordinate $Z$.

items.name: total_ion_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Total ion number density at the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient vanishes, summed over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation: The total ion number density at the magnetic axis is the local number density of all ion species, including every ionic charge state. The magnetic axis is the innermost point of the nested closed flux surfaces, defined by a vanishing gradient of the poloidal magnetic flux. At the magnetic-axis position, the quantity is defined by $$ n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) = \sum_s \sum_Z n_{s,Z}(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}) $$ where $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the magnetic-axis position, $s$ indexes ion species, and $Z$ indexes their ionic charge states. This is the all-ion aggregate of ion density at magnetic axis; it excludes electrons and neutral particles.

items.name: volume_averaged_effective_charge
items.description: Dimensionless volume-averaged effective ionic charge of a plasma mixture, formed by averaging the local second ionic charge moment normalized by free-electron density over the confined plasma volume.
items.documentation: Volume-averaged effective ionic charge is the effective charge of the complete ion mixture after spatially averaging the local charge-weighted ionic charge moment over the confined plasma volume. The defining relation is $$ Z_{\mathrm{eff},V} = \frac{1}{V_p}\int_{V_p} Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{eff},V}$ is the volume-averaged effective charge, $Z_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [effective charge](name:effective_charge), $V_p$ is the confined plasma volume, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $dV$ is the volume element. The average applies to the complete included ion mixture at every position, with ionic contributions summed over all represented species and charge states. It covers the confined plasma volume and is not restricted to one species, one charge state, one region, or one flux surface; it is distinct from an ordinary ion charge average. This quantity is the volume-averaged counterpart of [effective charge](name:effective_charge). It differs from flux-surface-averaged effective charge at the plasma boundary, which averages the local effective charge over a boundary surface, and from [volume-averaged ion charge](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge), which represents an ordinary ion charge number rather than the second charge moment normalized by free-electron density.

items.name: current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
items.description: Full current-density vector arising from the divergence of the parallel viscous stress tensor in a magnetized plasma.
items.documentation: Full current-density vector arising from the divergence of the parallel viscous stress tensor in a magnetized plasma. It is the current-density contribution associated with the parallel part of viscous momentum transport, where parallel refers to the magnetic-field direction in the stress tensor rather than to the direction of the resulting current. The perpendicular force-balance drift produced by the parallel-viscous force density is $$ \mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel} = \frac{(\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel) \times \mathbf{B}}{B^2} $$ where $\mathbf{J}_{\Pi_\parallel}$ is this current-density vector, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel$ is the parallel viscous stress tensor, $\nabla \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_\parallel$ is the corresponding viscous force density, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, and $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is the magnetic-field magnitude. Only the full tensor divergence enters this relation; it is not a scalar-viscosity definition. The vector direction is governed by the right-hand rule applied to the parallel-viscous force density and the magnetic field, and the contribution is locally perpendicular to $\mathbf{B}$. This quantity excludes current density due to [perpendicular viscous stress](name:current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), including its [field-aligned projection](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity), and the separate [heat-viscosity contribution](name:current_density_due_to_heat_viscosity). Directional projections include the [radial](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), [toroidal](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), and [vertical](name:vertical_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) components along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle increasing counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height, and the [poloidal component](name:poloidal_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) in the plane spanned by $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$. Aggregate viscous-current components such as [radial_current_density_due_to_viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) and toroidal_current_density_due_to_viscosity combine this contribution with perpendicular-viscosity contributions.

items.name: ion_charge_state_particle_flux
items.description: Ion charge-state particle flux is the signed net flow of thermal and nonthermal ions of one species and charge state through an oriented surface per unit area and time.
items.documentation: Ion charge-state particle flux is the net number flow of ions of one specified species and ionization charge state through an oriented surface per unit area and time. It includes thermal and nonthermal ions without selecting a fixed geometric or magnetic-field direction. For a local oriented surface, the defining particle-number moment is: $$ \Gamma_{s,q} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}})\,f_{s,q}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v $$ where $\Gamma_{s,q}$ is the particle flux for ion species $s$ and ionic charge number $q$, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen surface-normal unit vector, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $f_{s,q}$ is the particle-number distribution in position and velocity for that species and charge state. The symbols $\mathbf{x}$ and $t$ denote position and time, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element; the integral includes all velocities. Thermal and nonthermal contributions are added within the specified charge state, but different charge states are not summed. The quantity counts particles rather than their charge or energy. It is a net flux density, not a surface-integrated crossing rate or a one-way incident flux. No spatial averaging is intrinsic to the general definition; the flux-surface-normal specialization additionally uses a surface average. Summing over all ionic charge states of the same species, with the same orientation and averaging convention, gives the [ion particle flux](name:ion_particle_flux). The [parallel component](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) selects the local magnetic-field direction as the surface normal, whereas the [poloidal component](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_particle_flux) selects the local poloidal direction. Sign convention: Positive when net ion transport follows the chosen surface-normal direction.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_polarizer
items.description: Vertical coordinate of a polarizer is the signed Z position of the polarizer geometric center in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: Vertical coordinate of a polarizer is the $Z$ coordinate of the polarizer geometric center in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coordinate is the vertical component of the position of that center: $$ z_{\mathrm{pol}} = Z(\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{pol}}) $$ where $z_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the vertical coordinate of the polarizer and $\mathbf{r}_{\mathrm{pol}}$ is the position vector of the polarizer geometric center. This quantity applies to the polarizer element itself and only to its geometric center. It is not a vertical extent, surface normal component, orientation angle, or local tangential coordinate of the polarizer. Together with the [radial coordinate of a polarizer](name:radial_coordinate_of_polarizer) and [toroidal coordinate of a polarizer](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_polarizer), it specifies the polarizer center position in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Sign convention: Positive when the polarizer geometric center lies in the $+\hat{Z}$ direction from the vertical origin.

items.name: toroidal_angular_width_of_camera
items.description: Full angular span of a camera field of view in the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, equal to the non-negative difference between the largest and smallest unwrapped toroidal viewing angles.
items.documentation: Full angular span of a camera field of view in the toroidal direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is the non-negative difference between the largest and smallest limiting signed toroidal viewing angles subtended by the camera acceptance. In this frame $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$, and $Z$ is vertical height. Let $\phi_{\min}$ and $\phi_{\max}$ be the minimum and maximum unwrapped signed toroidal viewing angles of the limiting accepted rays. The toroidal angular width is defined by: $$ \Delta\phi_\mathrm{cam} = \phi_{\max} - \phi_{\min} $$ where $\Delta\phi_\mathrm{cam}$ is the toroidal angular width of the camera and the extrema are taken over the camera field-of-view boundary after choosing a continuous branch of $\phi$. This quantity describes only the toroidal extent of the field of view. It excludes the central toroidal pointing angle, the detailed field-of-view footprint or optical distortion, and the complementary [vertical angular width](name:vertical_angular_width_of_camera).

items.name: breakdown_initial_time
items.description: Timestamp at which plasma breakdown begins and discharge current starts to flow.
items.documentation: Timestamp at which plasma breakdown begins and discharge current starts to flow.

items.name: total_ion_decay_length_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description: Positive e-folding distance for the outward decrease of total ion number density across magnetic flux surfaces in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation: This quantity is the positive cross-field decay length of the total ion number density in the scrape-off layer. It is the species- and charge-state-summed specialization of ion decay length over the scrape-off layer. $$ \lambda_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \left|\frac{1}{n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}\frac{\partial n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}}{\partial \ell_\perp}\right|^{-1} $$ Here $n_{i,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total ion number density, summed over the included ion species and charge states, and $\ell_\perp$ is outward distance normal to magnetic flux surfaces, measured in m. The quantity excludes electron and neutral-particle densities and is non-negative by definition.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_lower_hybrid_antenna_row
items.description: Toroidal-angle coordinate of the middle reference position of a lower-hybrid antenna row in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The toroidal coordinate $\phi$ locates the middle reference position of a lower-hybrid antenna row around the machine symmetry axis. It is the angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. This coordinate specifies the row's toroidal location and does not determine its radial or vertical location. The corresponding radial location is given by the radial coordinate of the lower-hybrid antenna row. Sign convention: Positive when $\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above along the $+Z$ direction.

items.name: implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate
items.description: Rate coefficient multiplying the primary ion momentum quantity to represent its implicit source or sink contribution in transport equations.
items.documentation: This quantity is the coefficient for the implicit contribution to an ion momentum source term. It represents proportional momentum addition or removal associated with the primary ion momentum quantity, without selecting a particular directional component. The implicit source contribution is defined by $$ S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} = C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}} M_i $$ where $S_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit ion momentum source contribution, $C_{M,i}^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is this rate coefficient, and $M_i$ is the primary ion momentum quantity to which the coefficient is applied. The quantity applies to ion momentum and is independent of the component or direction selected by a specialization. It describes the coefficient itself, not the resulting momentum source and not the primary momentum quantity. A positive coefficient represents proportional momentum sourcing, whereas a negative coefficient represents proportional momentum removal. It is the implicit, proportional component of the broader [ion momentum source rate](name:ion_momentum_source_rate). The [toroidal implicit ion momentum source rate](name:toroidal_implicit_ion_momentum_source_rate) is a directional specialization in which the same coefficient concept is applied to the toroidal ion momentum quantity.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_total_ion_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of all charged ion species at the plasma boundary, summed over charge states and excluding neutral particles.
items.documentation:

It is a flux-surface average rather than a local point value, a volume average, or a neutral-inclusive density. items.name: poloidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna
items.description: Signed dimensionless poloidal component of the launched lower-hybrid wave refractive-index vector, measured along increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point.
items.documentation: The poloidal launched-wave index is the projection of the lower-hybrid launched wave refractive-index vector onto the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle about the antenna reference point. It describes the poloidal part of the launch spectrum and is distinct from the corresponding [toroidal launched-wave index](name:toroidal_launched_wave_index_of_lower_hybrid_antenna). The index is defined by $$ N_\theta = \frac{\mathbf{k}\cdot\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta}{k_0} = \frac{k_\theta}{k_0} $$ where $\mathbf{k}$ is the launched wave vector, $\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}_\theta$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$, $k_\theta$ is the corresponding wave-vector projection, and $k_0 = \omega/c$ is the free-space wavenumber for angular frequency $\omega$ and speed of light $c$. The projection is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The quantity describes the launch condition only; it is not the local poloidal wave index after propagation or interaction with the plasma. Sign convention: Positive when the launched wave-vector projection points in the direction of increasing geometric poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: deuterium_deuterium_emissivity_due_to_fusion
items.description: Local volumetric rate of neutron production from deuterium-deuterium fusion reactions, giving the spatial distribution of D-D neutron emission per unit volume at each point in the plasma.
items.documentation: The deuterium-deuterium neutron emissivity $\varepsilon_{DD}$ is the local number of neutrons produced per unit volume per unit time from D-D fusion reactions. Only the neutron-emitting D-D branch contributes, so this quantity is the local source of prompt fusion neutrons from deuterium-deuterium reactions that produce a neutron. For identical deuterium reactants, the branch emissivity is given by: $$ \varepsilon_{DD} = \frac{1}{2} n_D^2 \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DD,n} $$ where $\varepsilon_{DD}$ is the deuterium-deuterium neutron emissivity, $n_D$ is the local deuterium reactant number density, $\sigma$ is the fusion cross-section for the neutron-emitting D-D branch, $v$ is the relative speed of the deuterium reactants, and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DD,n}$ is the velocity average of $\sigma v$ over the local reactant distributions. The factor $1/2$ avoids double-counting unordered pairs of identical deuterium reactants. The scope is the D-D reaction channel at a plasma location, aggregated over all deuterium reactant charge states and kinetic populations that contribute to the local neutron-emitting D-D branch unless a component-resolved quantity is specified. It excludes the proton-emitting D-D branch, subsequent D-T neutron production involving tritium born from D-D reactions, and the [deuterium-tritium neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion). The reaction-pair label deuterium_deuterium denotes two deuterium reactants; it is not a charge-state-resolved fuel-state quantity. Integrating $\varepsilon_{DD}$ over a plasma volume gives the D-D contribution to the global neutron flux for the same reactant population, and weighting that contribution by the branch neutron energy gives its contribution to total neutron power. When reactant populations are resolved, the corresponding global neutron production can be decomposed into [thermal neutron flux](name:total_neutron_source_rate_due_to_thermal_fusion), beam-thermal neutron flux, and beam-beam neutron flux contributions; those are population decompositions of the volume-integrated source, not separate definitions of the local D-D emissivity. Together with [deuterium-tritium neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:deuterium_tritium_emissivity_due_to_fusion), this quantity is a reaction-channel-specific member of [neutron emissivity due to fusion](name:neutron_emissivity_due_to_fusion).

items.name: floating_electrostatic_potential
items.description: Electrostatic potential of an electrically floating Langmuir-probe collector relative to a chosen electrical reference, at which the net electric current to the collector vanishes.
items.documentation: This quantity is the electrostatic potential of an electrically floating Langmuir-probe collector, relative to a chosen electrical reference. It is a current-balance-constrained value of [electrostatic potential](name:electrostatic_potential), specifying electrostatic interaction energy per positive test charge at the collector. The defining floating condition is $$ I_{\mathrm{net}}(V_{\mathrm{f}})=0 $$ where $V_{\mathrm{f}}$ is the collector's floating electrostatic potential relative to the chosen reference and $I_{\mathrm{net}}$ is the total electric current entering the collector, including particle collection and any emission contributions. Zero net current does not require the individual electron, ion, or emitted-particle currents to vanish. This quantity applies to an individual plasma-exposed collector, whether fixed or moving. It is not a wall-surface or magnetic-flux-surface average, and it does not denote an externally imposed collector bias. It is distinct from the [plasma electrostatic potential at a Langmuir-probe position](name:electrostatic_potential_at_langmuir_probe_position): a sheath can sustain a potential difference between the plasma and the floating collector. That difference is governed by current balance and depends on the electron temperature, particle distributions, and any emission contributions; no universal fixed offset is implied. The [fluctuating floating electrostatic potential](name:fluctuating_floating_electrostatic_potential) is the standard deviation of fluctuations of this quantity, rather than its signed value. Sign convention: Positive when a positive test charge has greater electrostatic potential energy at the floating collector than at the chosen reference.

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_torque_density
items.description: Local toroidal angular-momentum source density contributed by passing particles whose parallel motion follows the co-current direction.
items.documentation: This quantity is the local toroidal component of torque density contributed by the co-passing particle population. It gives the source rate of toroidal angular momentum per unit volume for that orbit class. The toroidal torque density is defined by $$ \tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} = R f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}} $$ where $\tau_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing toroidal torque density, $R$ is major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, and $f_{\phi,\mathrm{co}}$ is the toroidal force-density component on co-passing particles. The parent [co-passing torque density](name:co_passing_torque_density) includes the corresponding angular-momentum source without selecting this toroidal component. This is a local quantity, not a flux-surface average, and is distinct from the [toroidal counter-passing torque density](name:toroidal_counter_passing_torque_density), which resolves the opposite passing-orbit branch. Sign convention: Positive when the co-passing force increases toroidal angular momentum in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: field_line_length
items.description: Arclength of an individually traced magnetic field line during plasma initiation, resolving the field-line length distribution rather than reporting an average connection length.
items.documentation: This quantity is the geometric arclength of one magnetic field line traced during plasma initiation. It characterizes the distribution of individual field-line lengths associated with the evolving magnetic topology. For a field-line trajectory parameterized by $(s)$, its length is $$ L = \int_{s_0}^{s_1} \left\lVert \frac{d\mathbf{r}}{ds} \right\rVert ds $$ where $L$ is the field-line length, $(s)$ is the position vector along the traced magnetic field line, $s$ is a tracing parameter, and $s_0$ and $s_1$ delimit the traced segment. The quantity applies separately to each traced magnetic field line during the plasma-initiation phase; it is not an average, sum, or charge-state aggregation. It does not impose the open-field-line averaging and closed-line replacement convention of [connection length](name:connection_length), and it is distinct from field-line fraction, which describes the fraction of lines that are open. The set of individual lengths provides a geometric characterization of magnetic topology, while the open-line fraction identifies the prevalence of open field lines within the same traced population.

items.name: neutral_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective particle diffusivity relating an internal-state-summed neutral population's diffusive flux to its opposing number-density gradient, without selecting a spatial direction.
items.documentation: The neutral diffusion coefficient characterizes particle transport driven by the local number-density gradient of an aggregate neutral population. It does not select a spatial direction, a particular neutral species, or a spatial region. For a Fickian closure along a chosen physical direction: $$ \Gamma^{0,\mathrm{diff}}_{s} = -D_0\,\hat{\mathbf{s}}\cdot\nabla n_0 $$ where $\Gamma^{0,\mathrm{diff}}_{s}$ is the diffusive neutral particle flux density along the unit direction vector $\hat{\mathbf{s}}$, $D_0$ is the neutral diffusion coefficient for that closure, and $n_0$ is the neutral number density. The operator $\nabla$ denotes the spatial gradient, and the superscript or subscript $0$ identifies neutrals. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for nonnegative diffusivity; choosing a direction for this relation does not impose isotropy. The number density and particle flux are summed over the internal states belonging to the specified neutral population, excluding charged particles. The effective coefficient is defined by the aggregate flux-gradient relation, not by summing internal-state coefficients. In contrast, the [neutral-state diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_state_diffusion_coefficient) applies to one specified internal state. This quantity excludes convective particle flux and is distinct from neutral energy or momentum diffusivity. Directional specializations, such as the [radial neutral diffusion coefficient](name:radial_neutral_diffusion_coefficient), apply the same particle flux-gradient relation to a specified direction.

items.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the nonnegative amplitude of a magnetic-field perturbation projected along the local equilibrium magnetic-field direction and divided by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. More specific names may add averaging conventions.
items.documentation: Normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude is the normalized amplitude of the component of a magnetic-field perturbation that is parallel to the local equilibrium magnetic field. It is a nonnegative scalar intensity formed from the absolute value of the parallel projection, not from the full perturbation vector magnitude. A representative definition is $$ \widetilde{B}_{\parallel,N} = \frac{\left|\delta\mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0\right|}{B_\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $\widetilde{B}_{\parallel,N}$ is the normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude, $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field perturbation, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}_0$ is the unit vector along the local equilibrium magnetic field, and $B_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference magnetic-field magnitude used for the normalization. This parent quantity fixes the parallel projection and normalization by a reference magnetic-field magnitude. It does not by itself fix temporal, spatial, spectral, or flux-surface averaging; those aggregation conventions are supplied only by more specific names. This quantity excludes the normalized total perturbation magnitude, perpendicular-to-field perturbation amplitudes, signed parallel perturbations, and unnormalized perturbation amplitudes. The absolute value in the definition makes the parent a magnitude, so reversal of the perturbation sign along the equilibrium field does not change its value. A concrete child such as [time-averaged normalized perturbed parallel magnetic-field magnitude](name:time_averaged_normalized_perturbed_parallel_magnetic_field_magnitude) adds a time-average aggregation to the same parallel-projected normalized magnitude; it is not a change from parallel projection to total-field normalization.

items.name: minimum_gas_flow
items.description: Minimum gas flow is the smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower bound of its controllable range.
items.documentation: Minimum gas flow is the lower reliable operating limit of the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It identifies the smallest controllable value of the aggregate gas stream throughput, rather than a molecular-species flow or particle-number rate. The pressure-volume throughput represented by this quantity is defined as $$ Q_g = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt} $$ where $Q_g$ is gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is gas pressure at the flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing that boundary, and $t$ is time. This quantity applies to the aggregate gas stream delivered through an injection system across a defined flow boundary. The stream is not restricted to a particular molecular species or charge state, and this quantity is distinct from mass flow and particle-number rate. Its defining distinction is the lower reliable operating bound, rather than an unrestricted instantaneous throughput. The gas flow quantity defines the same pressure-volume throughput without imposing a lower-limit condition; minimum gas flow is its lower reliable operating bound. Conversely, [maximum gas flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) is the upper reliable operating bound, so the two quantities delimit the controllable range rather than represent different throughput definitions.

items.name: vertical_electron_velocity
items.description: Signed height-axis component of the local electron-fluid bulk flow in the edge plasma, parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation: The vertical electron velocity is the height-axis projection of the local bulk electron flow in the edge plasma. It represents directed electron motion after averaging over particle velocities, rather than random thermal motion. The defining projection is $$ u_{e,Z} = \mathbf{u}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $u_{e,Z}$ is the vertical electron velocity, $\mathbf{u}_e$ is the local bulk [electron velocity](name:electron_velocity), and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The underlying bulk flow is the particle-density-weighted mean electron velocity at each position; no spatial averaging is implied. This signed component is distinct from the electron speed, thermal velocity spread, and particle flux. The vertical direction is geometric and need not coincide with the local magnetic-field direction. Together with [radial electron velocity](name:radial_electron_velocity) and [toroidal electron velocity](name:toroidal_electron_velocity), it specifies the cylindrical components of the electron-flow vector. Sign convention: Positive when the electron bulk flow has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_temperature
items.description: Temperature of neutral particles in one specified internal state sets the energy scale of their random translational motion after subtracting that population's mean flow.
items.documentation: Temperature of neutral particles in a specified internal state characterizes their random translational kinetic energy relative to the bulk motion of that state-resolved population. The internal-state label selects a quantum or excitation state; it does not make this an internal-excitation temperature. A cold or hot neutral temperature is that of the named component alone; without the component it covers the whole neutral population of the selected species. Using temperature in its energy-equivalent form, the defining second-moment relation is $$ T_{0,a} = \frac{m_0}{3n_{0,a}}\int |\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}_{0,a}|^2 f_{0,a}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $T_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved neutral temperature, $m_0$ is the neutral-particle mass, $n_{0,a}$ is the number density of that population, $f_{0,a}$ is its velocity distribution normalized to that number density, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $\mathbf{u}_{0,a}$ is its [bulk translational velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity). The subscript $0$ identifies neutral particles, $a$ labels the specified internal state, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity applies locally to one neutral species in one internal state, without summing or averaging over internal states, species, or spatial regions. It excludes directed bulk kinetic energy and the energy stored in internal excitation. It is the state-resolved counterpart of [neutral temperature](name:neutral_temperature), retaining an internal-state restriction that the species-level quantity does not.

items.name: momentum_flux_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description: Momentum flux due to E cross B drift is the dimensionless scalar transport of a selected component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface by the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It fixes the drift mechanism and dimensionless status while abstracting over the momentum component, surface-normal direction, averaging, and choice of normalization reference supplied by concrete specializations.
items.documentation: Momentum flux due to $E\times B$ drift is the scalar transport of a selected component of linear plasma momentum across an oriented surface carried by the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, expressed in dimensionless form relative to a reference momentum-flux scale. It represents the $E\times B$ advective transport channel of momentum, not an unspecified or total momentum-transport channel. The dimensionless scalar component is the surface-normal advective flux of the selected momentum density divided by a reference momentum-flux scale: $$ \Pi_{\alpha}^{E\times B} = \frac{\left\langle p_{\alpha}\, \mathbf{v}_{E\times B}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}} \right\rangle}{\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}} $$ where $p_{\alpha}$ is the selected component of linear plasma momentum density, $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$ is the electric-field-cross-magnetic-field drift velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the chosen oriented surface normal, $\langle\cdot\rangle$ denotes the aggregation or averaging convention specified by the concrete quantity, and $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the reference momentum-flux scale relative to which the quantity is expressed. This quantity fixes two things: the driving mechanism is the $E\times B$ drift, and the quantity is dimensionless, being expressed relative to a reference scale. It abstracts over the remaining axes: the transported momentum component $\alpha$, the orientation of the crossing surface, the population or velocity-space contribution included in $p_{\alpha}$, the averaging convention, and the specific choice of $\Pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Concrete specializations fix these axes. This is a flux of momentum, not the momentum density itself, not a force or torque density, and not the full momentum-flux tensor. It excludes momentum transport carried by parallel streaming, magnetic drifts, diamagnetic flows, collisional viscosity, or external forces except where those effects are part of the selected momentum density or of the fields that determine the $E\times B$ drift. The [normalized momentum flux due to $E\times B$ drift](name:momentum_flux_normalized_due_to_e_cross_b_drift) is the specialization that explicitly designates a reference normalization as part of its identity; the present quantity is the mechanism-level abstraction under which any such normalized member sits, without itself selecting which reference scale, momentum component, surface, or averaging is used. Sign convention: Positive when positive selected linear momentum is advected by the $E\times B$ drift through the oriented surface in the direction of the chosen positive surface normal, or equivalently when negative selected linear momentum is advected opposite to that normal.

items.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_velocity
items.description: Signed major-radius projection of the mean translational velocity of neutral particles in one specified internal quantum or energy state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the major-radius component of the [neutral internal-state velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_velocity) of one neutral species in one specified quantum or energy state. It represents directed bulk motion after averaging over particle velocities within that state. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the component is defined by: $$ u_{0,a,R}=\hat{R}\cdot\mathbf u_{0,a}=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{R})f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{0,a,R}$ is the major-radius velocity component, $\mathbf u_{0,a}$ is the state-resolved bulk velocity vector, $0$ identifies neutral particles, and $a$ identifies the specified internal state. The function $f_{0,a}$ is the phase-space number density of the selected neutral species in that state, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The coordinate $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. The average retains internal-state resolution and does not combine different states or neutral species. It is a signed vector projection, not the flow speed, thermal velocity spread, or particle flux. The major-radius direction need not coincide with the magnetic-flux-surface normal. The corresponding [radial neutral velocity](name:radial_neutral_velocity) combines internal-state contributions through a number-density-weighted mean; this quantity retains the contribution of the specified state. Sign convention: Positive when the state-resolved neutral bulk motion has a component away from the toroidal symmetry axis, toward increasing major radius.

items.name: parallel_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity
items.description: Parallel current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed magnetic-field-aligned projection of the electric current contribution associated with parallel viscous stress.
items.documentation: Parallel current density due to parallel viscosity is the signed local projection of the current contribution associated with the divergence of parallel viscous stress onto the magnetic-field direction. The two uses of parallel distinguish the current projection from the viscous-stress mechanism. For a nonzero magnetic field, the defining projection is: $$ j_\parallel^{(\mathrm{pv})} = \mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}\cdot\frac{\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|} $$ where $j_\parallel^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the parallel current-density contribution, $\mathbf{j}^{(\mathrm{pv})}$ is the full [current-density vector due to parallel viscosity](name:current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity), $\mathbf{B}$ is the local magnetic-field vector, and $|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude. The superscript $\mathrm{pv}$ identifies the parallel-viscosity contribution. In the magnetized edge plasma, this is a local, mechanism-resolved contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the total parallel current density or a flux-surface average. It excludes the perpendicular-viscosity contribution, whose field-aligned projection is [parallel current density due to perpendicular viscosity](name:parallel_current_density_due_to_perpendicular_viscosity). Parallel viscosity does not require its full current-density contribution to be field aligned. The [radial current density due to parallel viscosity](name:radial_current_density_due_to_parallel_viscosity) is a different projection of the same parent vector. Sign convention: Positive when the parallel-viscosity current-density contribution has a component in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: outer_radius_of_ferritic_element
items.description: Outer radial boundary of the annular cross-section of a ferritic element in the axisymmetric equivalent geometry, defining the external extent of the annulus centered at a reference point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The outer radius specifies the external boundary of the annular cross-section used to represent a ferritic element in the axisymmetric thick-line equivalent geometry. Ferritic elements are ferromagnetic inserts, and each element is represented by an axisymmetric body whose cross-section is an annulus centered at a reference point $(R_0, Z_0)$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius from the toroidal symmetry axis and $Z$ is vertical height. For an annular cross-section with inner radius $r_\mathrm{in}$ and outer radius $r_\mathrm{out}$, the enclosed area is $$ A = \pi\bigl(r_\mathrm{out}^2 - r_\mathrm{in}^2\bigr) $$ where $A$ is the cross-sectional area and $r_\mathrm{in}$ and $r_\mathrm{out}$ are radial distances from the annulus center. The constraint is $0 \leq r_\mathrm{in} < r_\mathrm{out}$. Together with [inner radius of the ferritic element](name:inner_radius_of_ferritic_element), this quantity defines the annular cross-section; [radius of the ferritic element](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid) specifies its radial placement rather than its outer boundary.

items.name: y_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture
items.description: Signed y coordinate of the geometric center of a diagnostic aperture in the right-handed camera Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the signed Cartesian y coordinate of a diagnostic aperture's geometric center, measured from the origin of the right-handed camera basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It locates the aperture along the camera-frame y axis. The coordinate is defined by projection of the center position vector: $$ y_{\rm ap} = \mathbf{r}_{\rm ap} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}} $$ where $y_{\rm ap}$ is the coordinate value, $\mathbf{r}_{\rm ap}$ is the aperture-center position relative to the camera-frame origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector; the length quantities are expressed in m. This camera-frame coordinate is distinct from the radial and vertical coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Together with the [x coordinate of the diagnostic aperture](name:x_coordinate_of_diagnostic_aperture), it locates the aperture center in the camera frame. Sign convention: Positive when the aperture center lies in the positive y direction from the camera-frame origin.

items.name: argon_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron argon source rate delivered to the plasma vessel by gas injection systems, where each injected argon atom with Z = 18 contributes 18 equivalent-electron counts.
items.documentation: The argon source rate due to gas injection characterizes the instantaneous rate at which neutral argon with atomic number $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is admitted to the plasma vessel by gas injection hardware, expressed as an equivalent-electron count rate. The equivalent-electron convention counts each injected neutral argon atom as 18 equivalent electrons because neutral argon has 18 electrons; this is an inventory-accounting convention, not a statement about subsequent ionization or confinement. The defining relation for injected argon is: $$ \dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}} $$ where $\dot{S}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon equivalent-electron source rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the raw argon-atom delivery rate in atoms per second, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 18$ is the dimensionless atomic number of argon. This quantity is the argon-species member of [source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:source_rate_due_to_gas_injection). It is the instantaneous time derivative of the corresponding accumulated equivalent-electron inventory [accumulated_argon_count](name:accumulated_argon_count), and differs from raw gas-particle source rates by the factor $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}$. Sign convention: Positive when argon is delivered into the plasma vessel, increasing the equivalent-electron particle inventory.

items.name: boron_density
items.description: Elemental boron number density, summed over neutral atoms and all ionic charge states through fully stripped B5+.
items.documentation: Boron density is the elemental boron particle density, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included in one additive quantity. $$ n_B = \sum_{Z=0}^{5} n_{B,Z} $$ where $n_B$ is the elemental boron density, $Z$ is the boron ionic charge state with $Z=0$ denoting neutral boron, and $n_{B,Z}$ is the density of boron in state $Z$. The quantity is the underlying boron density field; [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density) and [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density) are distinct averages of it. It excludes no boron charge state but is not a charge-state-specific or charge-weighted density.

items.name: line_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Number density of free electrons averaged along a specified plasma chord with equal path-length weighting, excluding electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions.
items.documentation: Number density of electron The line average is defined by $$\bar{f} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L f\,dl$$ where $\bar{n}_e$ is the line-averaged electron density, $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density evaluated along the chord, $L$ is the positive length of the specified chord, and $l$ is distance along it. The integration interval and length denominator refer to the same chord segment. The electron population includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons over the full velocity distribution; electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded. The average uses equal path-length weighting, without additional density or volume weighting. Unlike [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), this quantity averages along a chord rather than over the plasma volume. It equals the local density everywhere on the chord only when that density is uniform. The [line-integrated electron number density](name:line_integrated_electron_number_density) is instead a column abundance; dividing that abundance by its corresponding path length yields this mean when both quantities refer to the same path. The [line-averaged xenon density](name:line_averaged_xenon_density) applies the same chord-mean operation to xenon ions rather than electrons. The [ratio of line-averaged electron density to Greenwald density](name:ratio_of_line_averaged_electron_density_to_greenwald_density) uses this electron chord mean as its numerator and is a separate normalized quantity.

items.name: parallel_neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless factor scaling the collisionless free-streaming cap on the magnetic-field-parallel component of neutral momentum flux in edge-fluid transport closures.
items.documentation: This coefficient sets the free-streaming upper bound on the parallel component of neutral-particle [momentum](name:momentum) flux in edge-fluid transport closures. Parallel denotes the local magnetic-field direction, used as a geometric reference without implying that neutral particles follow magnetic field lines. The limiting flux magnitude is defined by $$ \Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel} = \alpha^0_{\parallel}\Pi^{0,\mathrm{fs}}_{\parallel} $$ where $\alpha^0_{\parallel}$ is this nonnegative limiter coefficient, $\Pi^{0,\mathrm{fs}}_{\parallel}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming reference magnitude, and $\Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel}$ is the resulting upper bound. The superscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $\parallel$ denotes the magnetic-field-parallel component. The limited neutral momentum flux $\Pi^0_{\parallel}$ satisfies $|\Pi^0_{\parallel}|\leq\Pi^{0,\max}_{\parallel}$; limiting its magnitude does not reverse its direction. The free-streaming normalization and limiting function are specified by the transport closure, not by this coefficient alone. This quantity is the parallel directional component of the [neutral momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient), not the momentum flux itself or a momentum diffusivity. It applies to the selected neutral population without explicit internal-state resolution, unlike the [parallel neutral-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:parallel_neutral_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient). No summation or averaging rule for state-resolved coefficients is implied.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_density
items.description: Number density of ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic charge states and averaged over the confined plasma volume inside the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation: Number density of ion The volume average of the local [ion density](name:ion_density) is defined by $$ \langle n_i\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_i\,dV $$ where $i$ labels the specified ion species, $n_i$ is its local ion number density, $\langle n_i\rangle_V$ is its volume-averaged number density, $V$ is the confined plasma volume enclosed by the last closed flux surface, and $dV$ is a volume element. The species density is summed over all ionic charge states and includes thermal and nonthermal ions; neutral particles are excluded. This is a single-species particle number density, not an all-species total, electric charge density, or mass density. It is a volume mean rather than a local value or a chord mean. Multiplying this average by the confined plasma volume gives the total number of ions of the specified species within that volume. The [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density) is a species-specific instance of the same averaging definition.

items.name: parallel_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Parallel pressure is the kinetic-stress component along the magnetic field, including directed motion, carried by suprathermal particles on untrapped orbits whose orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposes the plasma current. Flux-surface averaging aggregates this same component without changing its orbit-class or parallel-component scope.
items.documentation: Parallel counter-passing fast-particle pressure is the component of kinetic stress along the local magnetic-field direction, carried by suprathermal particles on counter-passing orbits. Counter-passing particles are untrapped and have orbit-averaged toroidal motion opposite to the plasma-current direction; the uncentered moment includes directed parallel motion. The local component is the second velocity moment of the counter-passing suprathermal distribution: $$ p_{parallel,mathrm{cp,fast}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \sum_c m_s \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})} v_\parallel^2 f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is this pressure, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $c$ labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v_\parallel=\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{b}$ is the velocity component parallel to $\mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{b}$ is the unit vector along the local magnetic field, $f_{s,c}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the phase-space number distribution of fast particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\Omega_{\mathrm{cp},s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space subset at $\mathbf{x}$ associated with their counter-passing orbits, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The subscripts $\mathrm{cp}$ and $\mathrm{fast}$ denote counter-passing and suprathermal particles, respectively. The quantity applies to the suprathermal population and is summed additively over fast-particle species and all charge states. It excludes thermal particles, trapped particles, co-passing particles, and stress perpendicular to the magnetic field. The local component and its flux-surface average have the same population and orbit-class scope; the average aggregates the local component over a magnetic surface. This is the counter-passing contribution to [parallel fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_fast_particle_pressure), which includes parallel stress from other fast-particle orbit classes. Together with the [perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), it determines the [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure), the one-third trace of the kinetic stress for the same population: $p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{cp,fast}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}})/3$, where $p_{\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the counter-passing fast-particle pressure and $p_{\perp,\mathrm{cp,fast}}$ is the perpendicular counter-passing fast-particle pressure.

items.name: volume_of_flux_surface
items.description: Volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface, including the entire plasma interior from the magnetic axis rather than only a shell between neighboring surfaces.
items.documentation: Volume of flux surface The volume is defined by $$ V = \int_{\Omega} d^3\mathbf{x} $$ where $V$ is the enclosed volume, $\Omega$ is the spatial domain inside the selected magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, and $d^3\mathbf{x}$ is the differential volume element. The integration covers the entire interior from the magnetic axis to the selected surface and excludes regions outside it. The result is the total enclosed volume, not the volume of a shell between neighboring surfaces or the volume of material structures. The volume tends to zero as the selected surface contracts to the magnetic axis. It equals the [volume enclosed by the plasma boundary](name:volume_of_plasma_boundary) when the selected surface coincides with that boundary. Differentiating this cumulative volume with respect to the poloidal magnetic flux coordinate gives the [poloidal-flux volume derivative](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_poloidal_magnetic_flux_coordinate); differentiation with respect to the toroidal-flux coordinate gives the [toroidal-flux volume derivative](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Enclosed-volume increments provide the geometric integration measure that converts flux-surface-averaged densities into enclosed totals. A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: accumulated_ammonia_deuterated_count
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3), expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units per molecule.
items.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative number of neutral deuterated ammonia (ND3) molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, converted to an equivalent-electron count. It is the post-breakdown contribution to ammonia_deuterated_count, distinct from the prefill contribution [ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count](name:ammonia_deuterated_prefill_count). The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = (Z_{\mathrm{N}} + 3Z_{\mathrm{D}})N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} = 10N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}} $$ where $N_{\mathrm{eq,ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{ND_3}}^{\mathrm{post}}$ is the cumulative neutral-molecule count after breakdown, and $Z_{\mathrm{N}}=7$ and $Z_{\mathrm{D}}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and deuterium. This is a bookkeeping quantity, not the number of free electrons in the plasma and not an instantaneous injection rate.

items.name: implicit_electron_particle_source_rate
items.description: Implicit electron particle source rate is the coefficient multiplying electron number density to give the implicitly treated contribution to free-electron production or removal.
items.documentation: Implicit electron particle source rate is the signed coefficient of the density-proportional contribution to a decomposed electron particle source. Its designation identifies the contribution assigned to implicit treatment in the electron density transport equation, not a separate physical production mechanism. The source decomposition is defined by $$ S_e = S_e^{\mathrm{exp}} + S_e^{\mathrm{imp}} n_e $$ where $S_e$ is the [electron volumetric source rate](name:electron_volumetric_source_rate) being decomposed, $S_e^{\mathrm{exp}}$ is its additive explicit contribution, $S_e^{\mathrm{imp}}$ is the implicit electron particle source coefficient defined here, and $n_e$ is the free-electron number density. This coefficient applies to the electron population and the particular source contribution being decomposed; it does not imply aggregation over all source mechanisms. It excludes the additive explicit contribution. The coefficient itself is neither a volumetric source nor a volume-integrated production rate: its product with electron number density supplies the implicit volumetric contribution. The analogous [implicit ion particle source rate](name:implicit_ion_particle_source_rate) multiplies ion density instead. Sign convention: Positive when the implicit contribution produces free electrons, and negative when it removes them.

items.name: normalized_particle_perturbed_energy
items.description: Dimensionless vector of normalized energy-weighted velocity-space moments of a species' perturbed particle distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.
items.documentation: This quantity is the normalized particle energy moment of a species' perturbed velocity distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode. Its components use distinct squared velocity-direction weights while sharing an energy-weighted normalization from the corresponding unperturbed species distribution. For species $s$ and selected velocity direction or weighting component $a$, the normalized moment is defined by $$ \mathcal{E}_{a,s} = \frac{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v_a^2 v^2\,\delta f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v}{\int \frac{1}{2}m_s v^4 f_{0s}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v} $$ where $m_s$ is the species mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $v$ is its magnitude, $v_a$ is the selected velocity component, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle distribution, $f_{0s}$ is the unperturbed distribution, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The quantity is a particle moment, distinct from gyrocenter moments and from unweighted density or pressure moments. The [perpendicular normalized particle perturbed energy](name:perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_energy) is its perpendicular directional realization.

items.name: ion_charge_state_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Ion charge-state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed transfer of a selected linear-momentum component per surface area for one ion charge state, attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport.
items.documentation: Ion charge-state momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed flux density of a selected component of linear [momentum](name:momentum) for one specified charge state of an ion species, attributed to pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic transport. The transported momentum component and the surface-crossing direction are distinct specifications; neither a toroidal momentum projection nor a flux-surface-normal crossing direction is imposed. For the selected momentum component and oriented surface, the flux is defined by $$ \Gamma_{a,s}^{\mathrm{dia}} = \hat{\mathbf e}_a \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{dia}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n} $$ where $\Gamma_{a,s}^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is this momentum flux, $s$ labels the specified ion species and charge state, $a$ labels the selected momentum component, $\hat{\mathbf e}_a$ is its direction unit vector, $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the oriented surface-normal unit vector, and $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_s^{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic contribution to that state's momentum-flux tensor, with its first index denoting transported momentum and its second index denoting crossing direction. This quantity is the charge-state-resolved specialization of [momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It contains no sum over ion species or charge states, unlike the charge-state-aggregated [ion momentum flux due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_momentum_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). It excludes contributions from non-diamagnetic transport mechanisms and is not the total momentum flux. Sign convention: Positive when positive momentum in the selected component is transported along the oriented surface normal.

items.name: boron_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the boron ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local boron-ion count per physical volume, summed over all boron ionic charge states.
items.documentation: Particle number density of the boron ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local boron-ion count per physical volume at that location. It represents boron ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutrals, or another plasma population, and is summed over all boron ionic charge states. The defining relation is $$ n_{\mathrm{B,axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_{\mathrm{B}}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{B,axis}}$ is the boron ion number density at the magnetic axis, $N_{\mathrm{B}}$ is the number of boron ions summed over all ionic charge states, and $V$ is physical volume. The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the complete ionized boron population at that location and excludes neutral boron; it is neither a flux-surface or volume integral nor a density for another species. This is the boron-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the same locus and aggregation convention as [beryllium density at the magnetic axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), but represents boron ions rather than beryllium ions. It differs from [boron density at the internal transport barrier](name:boron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier), which is evaluated at a different plasma location.

items.name: power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of collisional energy exchange per unit volume for a specified plasma population, species, charge state, or internal state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the net local volumetric energy exchange caused by Coulomb collisions for a designated target population. It is positive for energy deposited in the target and negative for energy transferred from it. $$ P_a^{\mathrm{coll}} = \sum_b Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}} $$ where $P_a^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the target power density in W m$^{-3}$, $Q_{a\leftarrow b}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume from partner population $b$ to target $a$, and the sum includes the collision partners and subpopulations specified by the quantity's aggregation scope. The target may be a broad population, as in particle collisional power density, or a species, ion charge state, internal state, or electron population. Aggregated electron and ion quantities include the designated contributing species and states, whereas resolved quantities retain only their specified target, as in [ion charge-state collisional power density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and internal-state collisional power density. Sign convention: Positive when the designated target population gains energy from its collision partners.

items.name: tritium_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all tritium charge states.
items.documentation: Tritium ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local concentration of tritium ions at the core-side shoulder of the edge transport barrier. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{T}} = \sum_z n_{\mathrm{T}}^{z+} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the tritium ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{T}}^{z+}$ is the number density of tritium ions with charge state $z$, and $z$ is the positive integer charge state. For tritium, the physically ionized population has one positive charge state, so the sum reduces to the density of singly ionized tritium. The quantity applies only to tritium ions and is evaluated locally at the pedestal top, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is not a chord-, volume-, or species-averaged density, and it excludes neutral tritium and all non-tritium species. This is the tritium-specific component of [density at the pedestal top](name:density_at_pedestal_top), rather than the corresponding total or non-species-resolved density. The same tritium ion density concept evaluated at a different transport-barrier location is [tritium density at the internal transport barrier](name:tritium_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

items.name: edge_localized_mode_frequency
items.description: Rate of recurrent edge-localized mode events during an ELMing H-mode phase, expressing the cadence of pedestal-relaxation bursts rather than their amplitude or exhaust.
items.documentation: The edge-localized mode frequency is the event rate of recurrent pedestal-relaxation bursts during an ELMing H-mode phase. It characterizes the cadence of ELM events, not their amplitude, duration, expelled particle content, or transient energy. $$ f_{\mathrm{ELM}} = \frac{N_{\mathrm{ELM}}}{\Delta t} $$ where $f_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the ELM event frequency, $N_{\mathrm{ELM}}$ is the number of identified ELM events, and $\Delta t$ is the elapsed interval over which those events are counted. The interval must represent the ELMing phase being characterized; isolated events outside that phase are excluded.

items.name: accumulated_silane_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of silane molecules delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18 equivalent electrons per neutral SiH4 molecule.
items.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral silane (SiH4) molecules delivered by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented on an equivalent-electron basis. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{eq}} = 18N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}} $$ where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron count and $N_{\mathrm{SiH_4}}$ is the cumulative number of neutral silane molecules delivered after breakdown. The factor 18 is the sum of silicon's 14 atomic-number electrons and four hydrogen atoms' one atomic-number electron each. The scope is silane delivered after plasma breakdown specifically by gas injection. The count is cumulative over all such delivery and is not an instantaneous rate, a count of free electrons in the plasma, or a charge-state-resolved inventory; subsequent ionization, transport, retention, and removal do not change the delivered-inventory convention. The corresponding instantaneous quantity is the [silane source rate](name:silane_source_rate). Like the [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), this quantity uses an equivalent-electron aggregation, but silane contributes 18 equivalent electrons per molecule rather than one per hydrogen atom.

items.name: y_second_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description: Signed y-axis direction cosine of the unit vector along a strain gage’s second measurement direction in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation: This quantity is the y-axis direction cosine of the unit vector defining a strain gage’s second measurement direction. For a strain rosette, it describes the orientation of that local sensing axis, not the gage’s spatial location. The component is defined by $$ d_y = \hat{\mathbf{d}}_2 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{y}} $$ where $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_2$ is the unit vector along the second measurement direction and $\hat{\mathbf{y}}$ is the positive y-axis unit vector of the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. Its value is one component of the orientation represented by the corresponding x-axis second measurement direction and z-axis second measurement direction. It is distinct from the [y coordinate of the sensor attachment point](name:y_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point), which locates the gage rather than specifying its orientation. Sign convention: Positive when the second measurement direction has a component toward increasing y.

items.name: focal_length_of_line_of_sight
items.description: Paraxial focal length of the collector optics associated with a charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight, setting the distance from the principal plane to the focal point.
items.documentation: The focal length is the paraxial distance from the principal plane of the collector optical system to the focal point for collimated incident rays. It characterizes the focusing geometry associated with a selected charge-exchange spectroscopy line of sight. This quantity applies to the collector optics of that line of sight and is not the diameter of the focused image spot or the optical throughput. The diameter of the line of sight describes the focused spot size, while the [etendue of the line of sight](name:etendue_of_line_of_sight) describes its accepted optical phase space; both are related to, but distinct from, focal length.

items.name: hard_xray_brightness
items.description: Band-integrated hard X-ray photon radiance received by a channel, normalized by projected collecting area and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation: Hard X-ray brightness is the photon radiance received from a viewing direction by a channel.
