It represents photon arrival rate with the photon-energy dependence integrated over the selected hard X-ray band. The band-integrated photon radiance is defined by $$ B_{\mathrm{HX}} = \frac{dN_\gamma}{dt\,dA_{\mathrm{proj}}\,d\Omega} $$ where $B_{\mathrm{HX}}$ is the hard X-ray brightness, $N_\gamma$ is the number of received photons in the selected energy band, $t$ is time, $A_{\mathrm{proj}}$ is projected collecting area, and $\Omega$ is accepted solid angle. This quantity applies to hard X-ray photons received by a channel and is evaluated separately for each selected energy band. Its aggregation convention is integration over photon energy within that band while retaining normalization by projected area and solid angle. It is a received radiometric quantity, not a local volumetric source term, and it counts photons rather than their deposited or carried energy. The local production counterpart is hard X-ray emissivity, which describes photon generation per unit volume and solid angle before propagation to the channel. Integrating this brightness over the collecting geometry represented by the [etendue of a hard X-ray detector](name:etendue_of_hard_xray_detector) gives the received photon rate under the corresponding angular and area acceptance. Unlike [incident soft X-ray radiance](name:incident_soft_xray_radiance), which is energy-weighted, this quantity is photon-count radiance; photon registration probability is a separate detector property described by [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector).

items.name: radial_effective_ion_diffusivity
items.description: Effective Fickian coefficient relating the radial diffusive flux of the charge-state-summed ion population to its total particle-density gradient.
items.documentation: The radial effective ion diffusivity is the Fickian transport coefficient for ion particle diffusion in the radial direction. It applies to the ion population summed over all ionic charge states and is the radial component of [effective ion diffusivity](name:effective_ion_diffusivity). The defining relation is $$ \Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}\,\frac{\partial n_i}{\partial r} $$ where $\Gamma_{i,r}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the radial diffusive ion-particle flux, $D_{i,r}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is this effective diffusivity, $n_i$ is the total ion particle number density, and $r$ is the radial coordinate. The radial flux is positive away from the magnetic axis; consequently, a positive diffusivity gives flux down the total-ion density gradient. This quantity excludes convective, conductive, and source terms.

items.name: displacement_of_passive_structure
items.description: Displacement of a passive structure is the signed linear displacement of a selected point or defined surface target on a passive component relative to a reference configuration, projected along a defined positive direction.
items.documentation: Displacement of a passive structure is the signed scalar component of the motion of a selected material point, attachment point, or defined reference point on a passive structural component relative to a reference configuration. It is the passive-structure instance of mechanical displacement, not an absolute position, velocity, acceleration, or strain. The signed projected displacement is defined by $$ u(t) = \left[\mathbf{r}(t) - \mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_u $$ where $u(t)$ is the scalar displacement, $\mathbf{r}(t)$ is the current position vector of the selected point, $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ is the position vector of the same point in the reference configuration, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_u$ is the unit vector defining the positive direction of the displacement component. All vectors and the unit direction are expressed in the same right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ frame, with $\hat{z}$ vertical. The selected point, reference configuration, and positive direction are part of the semantic definition of any instance. An undeformed, surveyed, calibrated, initial, or previous-time configuration may serve as $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ only if that choice is fixed; changing it changes the displacement, and using a previous-time reference defines an incremental displacement over the interval. A single value describes one projected local displacement; deformation or strain requires spatial variation of displacement or a separate deformation measure. Sign convention: Positive when the selected point is displaced from $\mathbf{r}_\mathrm{ref}$ in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_u$.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex first-order perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction in the confined plasma, for a single toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis. It is not the cylindrical major-radius component.
items.documentation: Imaginary part of the radial perturbed plasma magnetic field is the imaginary component of the complex first-order magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the confined plasma. It applies to one toroidal Fourier mode in linear MHD stability analysis and to the radial coordinate component in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho, \theta, \phi)$. The complex radial component is decomposed into real and imaginary parts as: $$ \delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) = \delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) + i\,\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}(\rho,\theta) $$ where $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$ is the radial flux-coordinate component of the complex perturbed magnetic-field eigenfunction for toroidal mode number $n$, $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{re}}^{(n)}$ is the corresponding [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), $\delta B_{\rho,\mathrm{im}}^{(n)}$ is this quantity, $i$ is the imaginary unit, $\rho$ is the radial flux coordinate, and $\theta$ is the poloidal flux coordinate. The scope is the confined-plasma region for the specified toroidal mode; it excludes the perturbed magnetic field in the vacuum region, any sum over toroidal mode numbers, and any real-valued instantaneous perturbation obtained after applying a toroidal and temporal phase factor. The radial direction here is the coordinate direction associated with increasing $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$; it is distinct from the major-radius $\hat{R}$ direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity is a local eigenfunction component, not a flux-surface average, volume integral, or magnitude. Together with the [real part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part), this quantity forms the complex radial component $\delta B_{\rho}^{(n)}$. Together with the [poloidal](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_imaginary_part) imaginary components, it forms the imaginary vector part of the perturbed plasma magnetic-field eigenfunction. The overall complex phase of a linear eigenfunction is arbitrary, so a phase rotation mixes the real and imaginary parts while leaving the represented complex eigenfunction unchanged. Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary radial component points toward increasing radial flux coordinate $\rho$ in the flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ for the adopted complex eigenfunction phase.

items.name: lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description: Dimensionless Luce squareness parameter for the lower-inner (below-midplane, high-field-side) plasma boundary in a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, measuring its departure from the reference ellipse set by boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity.
items.documentation: The lower-inner squareness of the plasma boundary is the dimensionless Luce shape coefficient quantifying how much the lower-inboard quadrant of the last-closed flux surface deviates from the reference ellipse determined by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. The lower-inboard quadrant is the part of the boundary at smaller major radius and below the reference-ellipse center in a poloidal cross-section. In the Luce higher-order boundary parameterization, the lower-inner boundary contour at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is represented over the lower-inboard interval of the poloidal angle $\theta$ by the coefficient $\zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}$: $$ \begin{aligned} R(\theta) &= R_{\mathrm{geo}} + a\cos\!\left[\theta + \arcsin(\delta_{\mathrm{ref}})\sin\theta - \zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}\sin(2\theta)\right],\\ Z(\theta) &= Z_{\mathrm{geo}} + a\kappa_{\mathrm{ref}}\sin\!\left[\theta + \zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}\sin(2\theta)\right] \end{aligned} $$ where $R(\theta)$ and $Z(\theta)$ are the major-radius and vertical coordinates of the boundary point, $R_{\mathrm{geo}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{geo}}$ are the coordinates of the geometric center of the reference ellipse, $a$ is the boundary minor radius, $\kappa_{\mathrm{ref}}$ and $\delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$ are the elongation and triangularity entering the same reference boundary description, and $\theta=0$ labels the outboard midplane with increasing $\theta$ first moving toward $+Z$. The geometric center of the reference ellipse is not the magnetic-axis position unless those points coincide for the chosen boundary geometry. This quantity is restricted to the lower-inboard quadrant and excludes the upper-inboard quadrant represented by [upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary). It is a quadrant-resolved component of [inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary), distinct from the outer-side squareness components, and complements [elongation_of_plasma_boundary](name:elongation_of_plasma_boundary) and [triangularity_of_plasma_boundary](name:triangularity_of_plasma_boundary) in describing boundary shape beyond the reference ellipse. With the sign shown in the Luce representation, positive $\zeta_{\mathrm{LI}}$ moves the lower-inboard corner toward smaller $R$ and lower $Z$ relative to the reference ellipse, making that corner more rectangular; negative values make it rounder.

items.name: line_averaged_tritium_density
items.description: Chord-averaged number density of tritium ions, obtained by averaging local tritium ion density along a specified chord.
items.documentation: Chord-averaged tritium ion density is the path-length mean of the local tritium ion number density along a specified chord. It is derived from the local [tritium_density](name:tritium_density) and represents the chord-integrated fuel content normalized by chord length. $$ \overline{n}_T = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L n_T(\ell)\,d\ell $$ where $\overline{n}_T$ is the chord-averaged density, $n_T(\ell)$ is the local tritium ion density at path coordinate $\ell$, and $L$ is the chord length. The average includes the specified chord segment and is distinct from the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density) and from the corresponding helium-4 quantity [line_averaged_helium_4_density](name:line_averaged_helium_4_density).

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source
items.description: The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma.
items.documentation: The toroidal component of the area-normalized momentum source for a specified ion charge state represents directional momentum transfer in an edge plasma. It is resolved for one ion species and charge state rather than summed over charge states. The toroidal component is defined by $$ S_{\phi,i,q} = \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is the area-normalized momentum source for ion species $i$ in charge state $q$, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This quantity is the toroidal specialization of the charge-state-resolved vector [ion charge state momentum source](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_source). It represents net momentum transfer associated with ionization, recombination, charge exchange, and related collisional processes; unlike [toroidal ion momentum source](name:toroidal_ion_momentum_source), it is not summed over ion charge states. Its corresponding poloidal projection is [poloidal ion charge state momentum source](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_source). Sign convention: Positive when the sourced momentum points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: effective_turn_count_of_coil_conductor_element
items.description: Signed effective winding count used to weight the magnetic-field contribution of an individual poloidal-field coil conductor element.
items.documentation: The effective turn count is the signed winding multiplicity assigned to one poloidal-field coil conductor element for calculating its contribution to the plasma magnetic field. Its magnitude represents the effective number of turns attributed to that element, while its sign represents winding orientation. This quantity applies to an individual conductor element and is not the total turn count of a complete coil or coil system. It is an effective electromagnetic contribution rather than a purely geometric count of visible conductor revolutions, and it excludes the separate winding counts of magnetic-field probe coils. For a fixed element current and geometry, the element’s magnetic-field contribution scales with its effective turn count; reversing the count reverses the corresponding field contribution. The same signed-winding concept is used for a [poloidal magnetic-field probe turn count](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) and a [toroidal magnetic-field probe turn count](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe), although this quantity applies specifically to a poloidal-field coil conductor element.

items.name: current_of_antenna_strap
items.description: Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a plasma.
items.documentation: Current of antenna strap is the oscillatory electric current carried along an auxiliary-heating antenna strap during electromagnetic-wave coupling to a plasma. It is a scalar line-current quantity associated with the strap itself. The strap current is the current-density flux through an oriented cross-section of the same strap: $$ I_s(t) = \int_{S_s} \mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t) \cdot d\mathbf{S} $$ where $I_s(t)$ is the current of antenna strap at time $t$, $S_s$ is an oriented cross-section of that strap, $\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{x},t)$ is the electric current density in the strap at position $\mathbf{x}$ and time $t$, and $d\mathbf{S}$ is the vector area element whose orientation sets the positive strap direction. This quantity is scoped to an antenna strap, not to an arbitrary antenna conductor, feed line, matching network, or complete antenna system. It denotes current carried by the strap material and is not a voltage, impedance, launched power, absorbed power, or a sum over multiple distinct straps. [Wave current of antenna strap](name:wave_current_of_antenna_strap) is the radio-frequency-wave specialization of this strap current and characterizes the same strap-carried current with a specified wave-current representation, such as peak amplitude or root mean square. The parent quantity identifies the common antenna-strap current shared by such specialized names without replacing their representation qualifiers. Sign convention: Positive when conventional current has a net projection along the assigned positive direction of the antenna strap.

items.name: volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature
items.description: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all included species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged over the confined plasma volume.
items.documentation: The volume-averaged total ion temperature is the volume average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy. The volume average is defined by $$ \overline{T}_{i,\mathrm{tot}} = \frac{\int_V T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV}{\int_V dV} $$ where $V$ is the confined plasma volume, $dV$ is its differential volume element, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local quantity defined by [total_ion_temperature](name:total_ion_temperature). Species and charge-state density weighting is performed locally before the volume averaging. Unlike [line_averaged_total_ion_temperature](name:line_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity averages over volume rather than along a plasma chord.

items.name: etendue_of_hard_xray_detector
items.description: Geometric optical throughput of a hard X-ray detector’s optical system, determined by its effective collecting area and accepted solid angle.
items.documentation: Étendue is the geometric throughput of the optical system associated with a hard X-ray detector. It characterizes the angular and spatial acceptance that determines how incident radiation is coupled into the detector. The defining relation is $$ G = A\Omega $$ where $G$ is the detector étendue, $A$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega$ is the accepted solid angle. This quantity applies to the detector-level optical system and uses effective area and angular acceptance for the associated detector; it does not specify whether those properties arise from one or multiple optical elements. It is distinct from the detector’s linear dimensions, such as its [height](name:height_of_hard_xray_detector) and width, which do not determine optical throughput alone. Étendue provides the geometric factor relating incident [hard X-ray brightness](name:hard_xray_brightness) to radiation coupled into the detector and is the same physical optical-throughput concept represented by [etendue_of_spectrometer](name:etendue_of_spectrometer), with the owning optical system changed from a spectrometer to a hard X-ray detector.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_major_radius
items.description: Flux-surface average of reciprocal squared major radius, providing a geometric metric coefficient for parallel-gradient and neoclassical transport calculations.
items.documentation: This quantity is the flux-surface average of the reciprocal square of the major radius on a nested equilibrium magnetic flux surface. It is a positive geometric metric coefficient used in parallel-gradient operators and neoclassical and gyrokinetic transport equations. It is defined by $$ g_{m1}(\psi)=\left\langle \frac{1}{R^2}\right\rangle_{\psi} $$ where $g_{m1}$ denotes this metric coefficient, $R$ is the major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the surface, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\psi}$ denotes the flux-surface average on that surface. The quantity applies to the entire magnetic flux surface and has no species, field-component, or source-process restriction. Its aggregation convention is a flux-surface average of the local reciprocal-square geometric factor; it is not the reciprocal square of a flux-surface-averaged major radius. It is the flux-surface-averaged form of the pointwise [inverse of square of major radius](name:inverse_of_square_of_major_radius). It differs from the related [flux-surface-averaged inverse of major radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius), which averages the first reciprocal power of $R$ rather than its reciprocal square.

items.name: trapped_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume from trapped nonthermal particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation: Trapped thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate of kinetic-energy transfer from trapped fast or non-Maxwellian particles to thermal ions of one specified species and charge state. Trapped guiding-center trajectories undergo magnetic-mirror reflection rather than continuous passing transit. The trapped restriction applies to the donating distribution, not to the orbits of the receiving thermal ions. The contribution is the flux-surface average of the receiving population's kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator: $$ P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\rho) = \left\langle \sum_a \int \frac{1}{2}m_{i q}v^2 C_{i q,a}\!\left[f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}},f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}\right] \, d^3v \right\rangle_\rho $$ where $P_{i q,\mathrm{tr}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is this collisional power density, $\rho$ labels the magnetic flux surface, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $q$ is its specified ionic charge number, and $m_{i q}$ is the receiving ion mass. The vector $\mathbf{v}$ is the receiving ion velocity, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is its speed, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration measure. The distribution $f_{i q}^{\mathrm{th}}$ describes the receiving thermal ions, while $f_a^{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped part of the nonthermal donor distribution for species $a$. The operator $C_{i q,a}$ gives the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution due to that donor species. Brackets denote the normalized flux-surface average, equivalently the limiting volume average over an infinitesimally thin shell surrounding the surface. The donor sum includes the nonthermal species represented in the collisional exchange; the receiving contribution is restricted to one species and charge state and is not summed over charge states. This is an energy-exchange source or sink, not stored kinetic-energy density or energy transfer through ionization or internal-state transitions. Adding the [co-passing](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) contributions to this trapped contribution recovers the flux-surface average of the [thermal-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions), which includes all donor orbit classes. Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy from the trapped nonthermal particles to the receiving thermal ions; negative when energy is transferred in the reverse direction.

items.name: toroidal_ion_charge_state_torque_density
items.description: Toroidal component of the net angular-momentum source density acting on a specified ion charge state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the net torque density acting on a specified ion species in a specified charge state. It represents the local source or sink of toroidal angular momentum, without attribution to a particular transport or collisional mechanism. $$ \tau_{\phi}^{i,q}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q} $$ where $\tau_{\phi}^{i,q}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and $\boldsymbol{\tau}^{i,q}$ is the full torque-density vector for ion species $i$ and charge state $q$. The vector parent is [ion charge state torque density](name:ion_charge_state_torque_density). The quantity is a total over all contributing processes for the specified ion charge state; process-resolved contributions are distinct quantities. Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density vector has a component in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: neutron_flux_at_first_wall
items.description: Neutron-carried energy flux arriving at the plasma-facing first-wall surface, providing the carrier-specific local contribution to energy delivered from the plasma to first-wall material.
items.documentation: Neutron energy flux at the plasma-facing first-wall surface is the local rate of neutron-carried energy delivered per unit surface area. It is the neutron-specific contribution to the energy flux associated with plasma loading of the first wall. $$ q_n(\mathbf{x}) = \int_0^\infty E\,\Phi_n(E,\mathbf{x})\,dE $$ where $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron energy flux, $\mathbf{x}$ is a position on the first-wall surface, $E$ is neutron energy, and $\Phi_n(E,\mathbf{x})$ is the differential neutron number flux at that position and energy. This quantity is local on the first-wall surface, integrates over neutron energy, and includes only the neutron carrier. It is not integrated over the surface and does not include photon, charged-particle, or other plasma-wall energy carriers. It describes energy arriving at the surface rather than nuclear energy deposited throughout the wall volume, which is represented by [nuclear power density of breeder blanket layer](name:nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer). The quantity contributes to the total local energy flux represented by [flux_at_first_wall](name:flux_at_first_wall). The representative [neutron_flux_maximum_at_first_wall](name:neutron_flux_maximum_at_first_wall) is obtained by taking the maximum of $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ over the relevant first-wall surface, while this parent quantity remains the local carrier-specific flux.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal
items.description: Signed coordinate of a Bragg-crystal outline vertex along the second local tangential axis of the crystal-local Cartesian (X1, X2) frame.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed position of a vertex on the Bragg-crystal outline, resolved along the crystal-local second tangential direction. It describes the crystal geometry in the local planar Cartesian frame $(X_1, X_2)$ rather than in the machine cylindrical frame. For a vertex position vector $\mathbf{r}$ and local-frame origin $\mathbf{r}_0$, the coordinate is defined by: $$ x_2 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_2 $$ where $x_2$ is the second local tangential coordinate, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the unit vector along the second local tangential axis, and $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the crystal-local frame. Together with the [first local tangential coordinate of the Bragg crystal](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_bragg_crystal), it specifies the in-plane location of the outline vertex. Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement from the crystal-local origin has a positive projection along the second local tangential unit vector $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states.
items.documentation: Particle number density of the oxygen ion population evaluated at the magnetic axis is the local oxygen-ion count per physical volume at that location, summed over all oxygen ionic charge states. It represents oxygen ions specifically, rather than electrons, neutral oxygen, or another plasma population. The defining relation is $$ n_{\mathrm{O,axis}} = \left.\sum_q \frac{dN_{\mathrm{O},q}}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{O,axis}}$ is the oxygen-ion number density at the magnetic axis, $q$ is an oxygen ionic charge state, $N_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number of oxygen ions in charge state $q$, and $V$ is physical volume. The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient vanishes. It applies to the oxygen ion population and is summed over all oxygen ionic charge states; neutral oxygen is excluded. It is a local density, not a flux-surface or volume integral. This is the oxygen-specific realization of the population-independent [density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It differs from [neon density at the magnetic axis](name:neon_density_at_magnetic_axis), which applies the same local, charge-state-summed convention to neon ions.

items.name: z_second_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description: Signed z-axis direction cosine of a strain gage’s second measurement-direction unit vector in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation: The second measurement-direction unit vector of a strain gage specifies the orientation of its second sensing axis. Its z-axis direction cosine is the signed projection of that orientation onto the Cartesian z axis. $$ d_{2z} = \hat{\mathbf{d}}_2 \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $d_{2z}$ is the z-axis direction cosine, $\hat{\mathbf{d}}_2$ is the unit vector along the second measurement direction, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector of the z axis in the right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame. For a unit direction vector, $-1 \leq d_{2z} \leq 1$. The second-direction component complements the z-axis direction cosine of the first measurement direction and is distinct from the [z coordinate of the sensor attachment point](name:z_coordinate_of_sensor_attachment_point), which specifies location rather than orientation. Sign convention: Positive when the second measurement direction has a component toward increasing $z$.

items.name: flux_at_limiter
items.description: Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. It fixes the limiter locus and the local surface-flux character; more specific quantities state the energy channel being carried, as in energy flux at limiter.
items.documentation: Flux at a limiter is the local surface rate density at which an energy-dimensioned plasma-borne quantity is deposited on the plasma-facing surface of a limiter. As a structural parent, it fixes the limiter locus and the local per-area rate character shared by its members, while each more specific name states the particular energy channel being deposited. For a local limiter surface element, the flux is the rate of the deposited quantity per surface area: $$ q_{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\partial^2 Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}}{\partial A_{\mathrm{lim}}\,\partial t} $$ where $q_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the flux at limiter, $Q_{\mathrm{plasma}\to\mathrm{lim}}$ is the energy-dimensioned quantity delivered by the plasma to the limiter surface element, $A_{\mathrm{lim}}$ is the area of that limiter plasma-facing surface element, and $t$ is time. The scope is restricted to plasma-facing limiter surfaces, and the quantity is local to the surface element: it carries no built-in integration, maximum, average, or other aggregation over the limiter unless a more specific standard name states such an aggregation. The carried quantity always has the dimension of energy, so every member of this family shares the same surface power-density character; the family does not extend to particle-count or momentum surface fluxes, which are dimensionally distinct quantities. This quantity excludes fluxes to non-limiter wall components, the total power deposited on a limiter, and signed vector heat-flux components normal to a surface. The more specific [energy flux at limiter](name:energy_flux_at_limiter) is the attested member that fixes the carried quantity as plasma energy deposition, inheriting the local limiter-surface rate-density semantics defined here.

items.name: neutral_pressure_of_mass_spectrometer_channel
items.description: Neutral pressure of a mass-spectrometer channel is the calibrated neutral-gas pressure equivalent assigned to a selected mass-to-charge channel. It denotes a channel-resolved neutral contribution and does not require correspondence to a unique neutral species.
items.documentation: Neutral pressure of a mass-spectrometer channel is the calibrated neutral-gas pressure equivalent assigned to one mass-discriminated channel of a mass spectrometer. The channel denotes a response in mass-to-charge space after ionization, so the quantity is a pressure equivalent for neutrals that can contribute to that channel, not a pressure of the detected ions. This quantity is neutral in scope: it excludes charged-particle plasma pressure, electron pressure, and any pressure contribution not represented as neutral gas before ionization. It is the neutral-specific counterpart of pressure of a mass-spectrometer channel. A channel value need not be the thermodynamic partial pressure of a single species, because fragmentation, isotopologues, charge states of produced ions, and isobaric species can overlap in the same mass-to-charge channel. Summing channel values represents [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure) only when the calibrated channels are non-overlapping, span the neutral mixture being represented, and treat cross-sensitivities consistently.

items.name: energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description: The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is distinct from the lower and upper bandpass-edge energies.
items.documentation: The energy of a detector pixel is the central or representative photon energy assigned to that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It is the energy counterpart of the [wavelength of detector pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel) and identifies the pixel's spectral-channel assignment rather than the finite width of its accepted band. For diffraction order $n$, the representative pixel energy is related to the pixel Bragg angle by Bragg's law and the photon energy-wavelength relation: $$ E_\mathrm{pix} = \frac{n h c}{2 e d \sin\theta_\mathrm{pix}} $$ where $E_\mathrm{pix}$ is the energy of the detector pixel, $n$ is the diffraction order, $h$ is Planck's constant, $c$ is the speed of light in vacuum, $e$ is the elementary-charge magnitude, $d$ is the spacing of the diffracting crystal planes, and $\theta_\mathrm{pix}$ is the Bragg angle associated with the pixel. This representative energy is the calibrated spectral-channel value selected by the spectrometer energy scale; it need not equal the arithmetic midpoint between the [lower bound energy of detector pixel](name:lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel) and the [upper bound energy of detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which define the edges of the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

items.name: area_of_flux_loop
items.description: The effective area of a flux loop is the non-negative field-to-flux sensitivity area of the sensor, including the aperture enclosed by each turn, the number of turns, and calibration factors. It converts a spatially averaged magnetic-field component normal to the loop aperture into total linked magnetic flux.
items.documentation: The effective area of a flux loop is the non-negative field-to-flux sensitivity factor of the sensor. It represents the aperture area enclosed by each turn, the number of turns, and calibration corrections that make the total linked magnetic flux equivalent to a spatially averaged magnetic-field component normal to the loop aperture. The effective area $A_\mathrm{eff}$ is defined by the relation between linked flux and averaged normal field: $$ A_\mathrm{eff} = \frac{\Phi}{\bar{B}_n} $$ where $\Phi$ is the signed magnetic flux threading the loop and $\bar{B}_n$ is the spatial average of the magnetic-field component along the chosen loop normal. For a specified loop normal and terminal polarity, Faraday's law gives $V = -d\Phi/dt = -A_\mathrm{eff}\,d\bar{B}_n/dt$ when $A_\mathrm{eff}$ is constant. Reversing the winding direction or terminal polarity reverses the signed quantities $\Phi$ and $V$, not the non-negative effective area. This quantity is the flux-loop analog of [area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe) for magnetic-field probes. It differs from [area_of_rogowski_coil](name:area_of_rogowski_coil), which describes coupling to enclosed current rather than linked magnetic flux; the corresponding signed circuit response is [voltage_of_flux_loop](name:voltage_of_flux_loop).

items.name: power_at_wall_due_to_convection
items.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by convective plasma particle flux, comprising thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic energy carried by streaming ions and electrons from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation: Convective power at plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces quantifies the energy transported by bulk plasma-particle flow from the scrape-off layer into the material surfaces. It comprises thermal enthalpy and directed kinetic-energy contributions and is the surface-integrated component of [power due to convection](name:power_due_to_convection). $$ P_{\mathrm{conv,wall}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wall}}} q_{\mathrm{conv}}(\mathbf{x})\,\mathrm{d}A $$ where $P_{\mathrm{conv,wall}}$ is the total convective power, $q_{\mathrm{conv}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local convective energy flux density at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $A_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the combined plasma-facing wall and divertor surface area included in the quantity. Only convective particle-energy transport is included; conductive and radiative deposition are excluded. [Power at a single divertor target due to convection](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_convection) isolates one target, while [convective power summed over divertor targets](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_convection) includes only the divertor-target subset. The conductive counterpart is [power at the wall due to conduction](name:power_at_wall_due_to_conduction).

items.name: plasma_velocity
items.description: Mass-weighted bulk center-of-mass velocity vector of the plasma fluid, whose projections onto the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) coordinate directions provide the radial, toroidal, vertical, and parallel flow components.
items.documentation: The plasma velocity is the local center-of-mass (barycentric) flow velocity of the bulk plasma, representing the momentum per unit mass carried collectively by all plasma species. It is the primary kinematic quantity in single-fluid and multi-fluid magnetohydrodynamic descriptions of plasma transport, rotation, and momentum confinement. The center-of-mass velocity vector is defined as: $$ \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{cm} = \frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s m_s n_s} $$ where the sum runs over all contributing plasma species $s$, $m_s$ is the species mass, $n_s$ is the number density, and $\mathbf{v}_s$ is the mean fluid velocity of species $s$. The full velocity vector decomposes into projections along the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame: the [radial component](name:radial_plasma_velocity) along $\hat{R}$, the [toroidal component](name:toroidal_center_of_mass_velocity) along $\hat{\phi}$, the [vertical component](name:vertical_plasma_velocity) along $\hat{Z}$, and the [parallel component](name:parallel_plasma_velocity) along the local magnetic-field unit vector $\hat{b}$. Individual projections are inferred from Doppler spectroscopy, charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, and motional-Stark-effect diagnostics; Mach probes provide parallel-flow access in the scrape-off layer.

items.name: runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density
items.description: Kinetic energy per unit volume carried by the runaway-electron population, including relativistic motion and excluding rest-mass energy.
items.documentation: Number density of runaway electron The local kinetic energy density is defined by: $$ w_{\mathrm{RE}} = n_{\mathrm{RE}}\left\langle (\gamma-1)m_e c^2 \right\rangle_{\mathrm{RE}} $$ where $w_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron kinetic energy density, $n_{\mathrm{RE}}$ is the runaway-electron number density, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{RE}}$ denotes a particle-number-weighted average over the local runaway-electron population. The Lorentz factor is $\gamma=(1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, where $v$ is electron speed, $m_e$ is the electron rest mass, and $c$ is the speed of light. Only the runaway-electron population is included, not the bulk thermal-electron population. The energy includes motion both parallel and perpendicular to the magnetic field but excludes rest-mass energy and electromagnetic-field energy. For a magnetic-flux-surface description, the quantity is the mean of the local energy density over each magnetic flux surface, not a mean over the entire confined plasma volume. It is an energy per volume, not a mean energy per electron. Its plasma-volume integral is the total [runaway-electron kinetic energy](name:runaway_electron_kinetic_energy), denoted $W_{\mathrm{RE}}$. Dividing that integral by the same plasma volume gives the [volume-averaged runaway-electron kinetic energy density](name:volume_averaged_runaway_electron_kinetic_energy_density).

items.name: outer_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak
items.description: Outward extent of the hard X-ray emissivity peak from its maximum to the outer half-maximum point toward the separatrix in normalized toroidal flux.
items.documentation: This quantity is the outward half-width of the hard X-ray emissivity peak, measured from the emissivity maximum toward the separatrix in normalized toroidal flux. It characterizes the radial spread of hard X-ray emission associated with nonthermal electrons on the outer side of the peak. $$ h_{\mathrm{outer}} = \rho_{\mathrm{half,out}} - \rho_{\mathrm{peak}}, \qquad \epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}(\rho_{\mathrm{half,out}}) = \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}(\rho_{\mathrm{peak}}) $$ Here, $h_{\mathrm{outer}}$ is the outward half-width, $\rho_{\mathrm{peak}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate of the hard X-ray emissivity maximum, $\rho_{\mathrm{half,out}}$ is the outer coordinate where the emissivity reaches half its peak value, and $\epsilon_{\mathrm{HX}}$ is the hard X-ray emissivity as a function of normalized toroidal-flux coordinate $\rho$. The quantity applies only to the outer side of the emissivity peak, with increasing $\rho$ directed toward the separatrix. It is a nonnegative extent and is distinct from the inward half-width, which measures the corresponding distance on the magnetic-axis side of the peak. Together, the two directional widths characterize the asymmetric spread of the peak; the [inner hard X-ray half-width at the emissivity peak](name:inner_hard_xray_half_width_at_emissivity_peak) provides the inward counterpart.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Poloidal component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, represented as a linear MHD eigenfunction and distinct from its radial and toroidal components.
items.documentation: The poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential is the poloidal component of the first-order departure of the plasma magnetic vector potential from its reference state. In linear magnetohydrodynamic eigenfunction descriptions, it carries the poloidal part of the magnetic-vector-potential perturbation without selecting a real or imaginary phase component. The perturbed magnetic field associated with the full vector potential perturbation satisfies $$ \delta \mathbf{B} = \nabla \times \delta \mathbf{A} $$ where $\delta \mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic field, $\nabla$ is the spatial gradient operator, and $\delta \mathbf{A}$ is the full perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential. The poloidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $R$ the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate. This quantity is restricted to the poloidal component and is not the complete vector potential, its radial component, its toroidal component, or the perturbed magnetic field itself. It is also distinct from the real-valued specialization [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential real part](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part), which selects one phase component of the corresponding eigenfunction. The component is a specialization of the full [perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential); its curl contributes to the associated perturbed magnetic field. A gage transformation can change the vector-potential representation without changing this curl, so the vector-potential component is not uniquely identical to a magnetic-field component. The radial component provides an adjacent component specialization of the same perturbed-vector-potential family.

items.name: lower_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel
items.description: The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy accepted by that pixel's spectral bandpass in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
items.documentation: The lower bound energy of a detector pixel is the minimum photon energy at the low-energy edge of the spectral interval accepted by an individual detector pixel in an X-ray crystal spectrometer. It defines the lower endpoint of that pixel's photon-energy acceptance range. This quantity applies to photons assigned to one detector pixel and represents a per-pixel spectral-channel boundary, not an integrated or averaged energy over multiple pixels or channels. It is distinct from the [energy of a detector pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which is the central or representative photon energy assigned to the pixel, and from the [upper bound energy of a detector pixel](name:upper_bound_energy_of_detector_pixel), which defines the high-energy edge. Together, the lower and upper bounds delimit the pixel's accepted photon-energy interval.

items.name: alfven_frequency
items.description: Alfvén frequency at a given radial position for a single toroidal mode number is the complex local shear-Alfvén continuum angular frequency; its real part gives oscillation and its imaginary part gives growth or damping for the stated time dependence.
items.documentation: Alfvén frequency at a given radial position for a single toroidal mode number is the complex local shear-Alfvén continuum angular frequency for perturbations propagating along the magnetic field on the flux surface at that radial position. Its [real part](name:alfven_frequency_real_part) is the oscillatory component, and its [imaginary part](name:alfven_frequency_imaginary_part) is the temporal growth or damping component. The ideal shear-Alfvén continuum relation defining the underlying continuum frequency is $$ \omega_A = |k_\parallel| v_A $$ where $\omega_A$ is the real continuum angular frequency, $k_\parallel$ is the component of the wave vector parallel to the magnetic field, and $v_A$ is the Alfvén speed, $B/\sqrt{\mu_0\rho_m}$ with $B$ the magnetic-field magnitude, $\mu_0$ the vacuum permeability, and $\rho_m$ the plasma mass density. This quantity denotes the full complex frequency $\Omega_A=\operatorname{Re}(\Omega_A)+i\operatorname{Im}(\Omega_A)$, not either component alone, and it is an angular frequency rather than a cyclic frequency. The radial position is a flux-surface label in explicitly named flux coordinates such as $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ or $(\psi,\theta,\phi)$, not a cylindrical vector component in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. At fixed toroidal mode number, $k_\parallel$ is determined by field-line pitch, magnetic geometry, and poloidal harmonic content, with the [safety factor](name:safety_factor) entering common single-harmonic specializations. Sign convention: Positive when $\operatorname{Im}(\Omega_A)$ makes perturbations proportional to $\exp(-i\Omega_A t)$ grow exponentially in time.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged rate of Coulomb-collisional kinetic-energy transfer to counter-passing fast particles from ions of one specified species and charge state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which Coulomb collisions with ions of one specified species and charge state change the kinetic-energy density of counter-passing fast particles. Counter-passing particles follow untrapped guiding-center trajectories whose parallel transit is opposite to the reference co-passing direction. The defining kinetic-energy moment is $$ P_{\mathrm{counter},bq}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \left\langle \int_{\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}} \frac{1}{2}m_a v^2 C_{a,bq}[f_a,f_{bq}](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle $$ where $P_{\mathrm{counter},bq}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the counter-passing collisional power density for ion partner species $b$ and ionic charge number $q$; $a$ identifies the fast-particle distribution species; $m_a$ is its particle mass; $\mathbf{x}$ is position; $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity; and $v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed. The functions $f_a$ and $f_{bq}$ are the fast-particle and ion-partner velocity distributions, respectively. The operator $C_{a,bq}$ gives the collisional time derivative of $f_a$ caused by that ion partner, $\Omega_{\mathrm{counter}}$ selects counter-passing phase space, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration measure, and angle brackets denote a magnetic-flux-surface average. The charge-state label identifies the ion collision partner, not a charge-state restriction on the receiving fast particles. This is a single-partner contribution, with no sum over partner species or charge states. It is a collisional source or sink, not stored kinetic-energy density or spatially integrated power. Together with the [co-passing contribution](name:co_passing_fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) and the trapped contribution for the same ion partner, it reconstructs the flux-surface average of the [all-orbit fast-particle collisional power density for that ion charge state](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions). Sign convention: Positive when collisions with the specified ion charge state increase the kinetic-energy density of the counter-passing fast-particle population; negative when they decrease it.

items.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Density-weighted toroidal bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier, resolved along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: Toroidal iron velocity at the pedestal top is the density-weighted mean bulk-flow velocity of ionized iron ions at the core-side shoulder of the H-mode edge transport barrier. It includes all populated iron charge states from Fe+ through fully stripped iron and excludes neutral iron. For charge states $q=1,\ldots,26$, the velocity is defined by $$ v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q u_{\phi,q}}{\sum_{q=1}^{26} n_q} $$ where $n_q$ is the number density of iron charge state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, $u_{\phi,q}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow component in m s$^{-1}$, and $v_\phi^{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the resulting density-weighted velocity. This charge-state aggregation is distinct from a charge-state-resolved velocity and is analogous to [toroidal krypton velocity at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_krypton_velocity_at_pedestal_top); its locus differs from [toroidal iron velocity at the internal transport barrier](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier). Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted iron-ion flow points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: krypton_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over krypton charge states and excluding neutral krypton.
items.documentation: Particle number density of krypton ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the krypton-ion population at that flux-surface location. The [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) is the parent quantity for this krypton-specific population. The number density is defined by $$ n = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N}{\Delta V} $$ where $n$ is number density, $N$ is the number of particles, and $V$ is volume. The quantity sums all ionized krypton charge states and excludes neutral krypton atoms. It is therefore an elemental ion density, analogous to the ion density at the internal transport barrier, rather than a density for one specified charge state. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport permits steep impurity-density gradients.

items.name: radial_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient multiplying the R-direction temperature gradient, in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, of neutral particles in a specified internal state in diffusive thermal-energy transport. It is internal-state-resolved and represents only the Fickian radial contribution.
items.documentation: Fick's-law radial neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient is the scalar radial diffusivity for energy transport by neutral particles in a specified internal state, and is the radial component form of the [neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Here radial denotes projection along $\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is resolved for one internal state, not summed or averaged over internal states. The radial Fickian contribution is defined by $$ q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,R} = - n_{n,s} D_{E,n,s,R} \frac{\partial T_{n,s}}{\partial R} $$ where $q^{\mathrm{diff}}_{E,n,s,R}$ is the radial component of the diffusive thermal-energy flux carried by neutral particles in internal state $s$, $n_{n,s}$ is their number density, $D_{E,n,s,R}$ is this coefficient, and $T_{n,s}$ is their temperature. The coefficient includes only the Fickian term driven by $\partial T_{n,s}/\partial R$ and excludes convective energy transport, sources, sinks, and effective coefficients that absorb non-diffusive contributions. It specializes the internal-state energy diffusion coefficient to neutral particles and is the internal-state-resolved counterpart of the [neutral energy diffusion coefficient](name:neutral_energy_diffusion_coefficient); it is distinct from the [poloidal neutral internal-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_neutral_internal_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). Sign convention: Positive when a negative radial temperature derivative produces a diffusive thermal-energy flux in the $+\hat{R}$ direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: temperature_of_sensor
items.description: Thermodynamic temperature associated with a selected thermocouple sensor attached to a tokamak structural component.
items.documentation: This quantity is the absolute thermodynamic temperature associated with one selected sensor member, represented by the thermal state at its thermocouple junction. It characterizes the local thermal condition of the attached structural component at the sensor location. For a system in thermodynamic equilibrium, temperature is defined by $$ T = \left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial S}\right)_{V,N} $$ where $T$ is thermodynamic temperature, $U$ is internal energy, $S$ is entropy, $V$ is volume, and $N$ is the amount of material or particle number held fixed in the derivative. The quantity applies to the selected sensor member individually and is not a sum, average, or other aggregation over the sensor set. It denotes the sensor or junction thermal state associated with a structural component, not the temperature of a flowing coolant or of an entire plant connection. It is distinct from [coolant temperature at inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet), which describes fluid entering a cooling system. Object-specific quantities such as [temperature of a coil conductor](name:temperature_of_coil_conductor) and [temperature of a neutron detector](name:temperature_of_neutron_detector) apply the same thermodynamic concept to explicitly named hardware rather than to the generic sensor locus.

items.name: line_averaged_oxygen_density
items.description: Line-averaged oxygen density is the line-of-sight mean of the local oxygen number density, summed over all charge states from neutral O0 through fully stripped O8+, along a specified chord through the plasma.
items.documentation: The line-averaged oxygen density is the line-of-sight mean of the local oxygen number density—summed over all charge states from neutral O$^0$ through fully stripped O$^{8+}$—along a specified chord through the plasma. It represents the oxygen impurity concentration averaged by arclength rather than the value at a single point. For a chord of length $L$, the line-averaged oxygen density is defined by: $$ \bar{n}_\mathrm{O} = \frac{1}{L}\int_0^L n_\mathrm{O}(\ell)\,d\ell $$ where $\bar{n}_\mathrm{O}$ is the line-averaged oxygen density, $L$ is the physical length of the chord segment included in the average, $\ell$ is arclength along that chord, and $n_\mathrm{O}(\ell)$ is the [local oxygen density](name:oxygen_density) at the point labeled by $\ell$. The scope is the species-level oxygen impurity population intersected by the specified chord: the density is charge-state-summed over neutral oxygen and all oxygen ions, and the spatial aggregation is an arclength average along the chord. It excludes charge-state-resolved oxygen densities, the local point value [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), and the spatial mean over the confined plasma volume. The essential relationship to [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density) is that the local charge-state-summed density is the integrand of the chord average. [Volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) is the analogous mean formed over a plasma volume, whereas this quantity is formed only along the specified line of sight and is normalized by the chord length.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_toroidal_current_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density is the net conventional toroidal charge flux per area, averaged over a closed magnetic surface with additional inverse-major-radius weighting.
items.documentation:
Flux-surface-averaged toroidal current density is the signed geometric toroidal component of the net plasma current density, averaged over a closed magnetic flux surface with additional inverse-major-radius weighting. The defining weighted average is $$\langle fangle = \oint f\,dS/|
abla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|
abla\psi|$$ where $j_\phi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ is this averaged current density, $j_\phi$ is the local [toroidal current density](name:toroidal_current_density), $R$ is major radius, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux labeling the selected surface. Angle brackets denote the flux-surface average, defined by $\langle fangle = \oint f\,dS/|
abla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|
abla\psi|$, where $f$ is the averaged quantity, $S$ is the closed magnetic surface, $dS$ is its area element, and $
abla\psi$ is the poloidal-flux gradient. The quantity includes the net contribution from all plasma current-carrying populations and mechanisms over the complete selected surface, including closed surfaces in the core plasma. It is neither a pointwise current density nor the total current through the enclosed plasma cross-section. The additional inverse-major-radius weighting distinguishes it from the ordinary flux-surface average $\langle j_\phiangle$. The underlying [current-density vector](name:current_density) is projected onto the geometric toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height. Unlike [flux-surface-averaged parallel current density](name:flux_surface_averaged_parallel_current_density), this quantity uses the geometric toroidal projection rather than a magnetic-field-aligned projection. Sign convention: Positive when the weighted net conventional current flows in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Local number density of nitrogen ions at the H-mode pedestal top, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral nitrogen.
items.documentation: Nitrogen ion number density at the H-mode pedestal top is the local number of nitrogen ions per physical volume, with all ionic charge states aggregated. The charge-state sum is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{N}} = \sum_{q=1}^{7} n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{N}}$ is the total nitrogen-ion number density, $n_{\mathrm{N}^{q+}}$ is the number density of nitrogen ions in charge state $q$, and $q$ is the positive integer ionic charge state from singly ionized through fully stripped nitrogen. This quantity applies locally at the inner shoulder of the H-mode edge pedestal, whose position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It is summed over nitrogen ion charge states and excludes neutral nitrogen; it is not a charge-state-resolved density or a flux-surface average. The locus distinguishes this quantity from [nitrogen density at the plasma boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary), which represents the same charge-state-summed nitrogen-ion density at the plasma boundary rather than at the pedestal top.

items.name: magnetic_shear_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Magnetic shear at an internal transport barrier is the normalized logarithmic derivative of the safety factor with respect to the outward normalized toroidal-flux radial coordinate at the internal-transport-barrier flux surface.
items.documentation: Magnetic shear at an internal transport barrier is the local magnetic shear evaluated on the flux surface identified as the internal-transport-barrier location. It characterizes the radial variation of field-line pitch through the safety factor at that locus. The defining relation is $$ s_{\mathrm{ITB}} = \left.\frac{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}{q}\frac{d q}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}}\right|_{\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}=\rho_{\mathrm{tor,ITB}}} $$ where $s_{\mathrm{ITB}}$ is the magnetic shear at the internal transport barrier, $q$ is the [safety factor](name:safety_factor), $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux radius used as an outward flux-surface radial coordinate, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,ITB}}$ is the value of that coordinate at the internal-transport-barrier location. The scope is the local value at the internal-transport-barrier flux surface in a magnetically confined plasma. It is not an average over the barrier width, not the position or width of the barrier, and not the magnetic shear at the pedestal top or another named flux-surface locus. Its aggregation convention is a single flux-surface evaluation with no averaging over neighboring flux surfaces. This quantity is a locus-specific specialization of [magnetic shear at a flux surface](name:magnetic_shear_at_flux_surface): it uses the same normalized logarithmic safety-factor derivative, with the flux-surface label fixed to the internal-transport-barrier location. The derivative is local in $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$, so the quantity represents the local radial slope of $q$ rather than an integral measure across the barrier. Sign convention: Positive when the safety-factor gradient with respect to increasing outward $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ has the same sign as the safety factor at the internal transport barrier.

items.name: radial_ion_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective Fickian diffusivity for total-ion particle transport, relating the radial diffusive flux across magnetic surfaces to the opposing radial gradient of charge-state-summed ion density.
items.documentation: Radial ion diffusion coefficient is the effective particle diffusivity for total ions moving radially across nested magnetic flux surfaces. It parameterizes Fickian radial mixing of charge-state-summed ion density. For radial transport, the defining relation is $$ \Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)} = -D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}\nabla_r n_i $$ where $\Gamma_{i,\mathrm{diff}}^{(r)}$ is the radial diffusive particle-flux component, $D_i^{\mathrm{eff},(r)}$ is the radial effective diffusivity, $\nabla_r n_i$ is the radial gradient of total ion number density, and $n_i$ is the ion density summed over all ionic charge states. The minus sign specifies transport down the density gradient. This is the radial member of the general [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) family. Neutral particles and charge-state-resolved coefficients, such as the [radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient), are excluded.

items.name: counter_passing_power_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for counter-passing particles, representing energy transfer to or from particles circulating opposite to the plasma-current direction.
items.documentation: Counter-passing power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is transferred to or from the counter-passing orbit population per unit physical volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of power density; counter-passing particles are passing particles that circulate opposite to the plasma-current direction, distinct from [co-passing power density](name:co_passing_power_density) and [trapped power density](name:trapped_power_density). For the underlying local energy balance, volumetric power density is defined by $$ p_{\mathrm{cp}} = \frac{dE_{\mathrm{cp}}}{dt\,dV} $$ where $E_{\mathrm{cp}}$ is the energy transferred to the counter-passing population, $t$ is time, and $V$ is physical volume. The flux-surface average is applied to this local rate while retaining its per-volume meaning. Positive values denote net energy gain by the counter-passing population; negative values denote net energy loss. Wave-particle interactions, collisions, and particle sources contribute when they are included in the counter-passing energy balance.

items.name: total_heating_power_due_to_fusion_reactions
items.description: Gross thermal power delivered to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric conversion cycle from fusion reactions, including blanket energy multiplication.
items.documentation: Total fusion-attributed heating power is the gross thermal input delivered to a fusion power plant’s thermal-to-electric conversion cycle. It combines heat released by fusion reactions with additional thermal power produced by nuclear energy multiplication in the blanket. $$ P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}} = P_{\mathrm{fusion}} + P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}} $$ Here, $P_{\mathrm{cycle}}^{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the total fusion-attributed thermal power supplied to the conversion cycle, $P_{\mathrm{fusion}}$ is the thermal power released by fusion reactions and entering the plant heat stream, and $P_{\mathrm{blanket}}^{\mathrm{mult}}$ is the additional thermal power generated by energy multiplication in the blanket. The quantity is aggregated over all included fusion-reaction and blanket-multiplication contributions at the plant conversion-cycle boundary. It is a gross thermal input, not local plasma heating or a power density. The cumulative plasma heating or energy-transfer quantity [power at an inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface) describes energy associated with a plasma region and is therefore distinct from this plant-level cycle input.

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Signed vertical projection of the pressure-gradient-driven diamagnetic fluid velocity for one ion charge state in the edge plasma, distinct from individual guiding-center motion.
items.documentation: The vertical ion charge-state diamagnetic-drift velocity is the signed projection of the pressure-gradient-driven fluid drift for one ion charge state in the edge plasma. It represents a fluid-moment contribution rather than the guiding-center motion of individual ions. For a magnetized ion charge state labeled $\alpha$ with scalar partial pressure, the defining projection is: $$ v_{\ast\alpha,Z} = \left(-\frac{\nabla p_\alpha \times \mathbf{B}}{q_\alpha n_\alpha B^2}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $v_{\ast\alpha,Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic-drift velocity component, $p_\alpha$ is the charge state's partial pressure, $\nabla p_\alpha$ is its pressure gradient, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$ is its magnitude, $q_\alpha$ is the signed particle charge, $n_\alpha$ is the charge-state number density, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the toroidal symmetry axis toward increasing vertical height. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Only the specified ion species and charge state are included; no averaging over charge states or species is implied. This contribution excludes electric-field drift, polarization drift, curvature drift, and independent parallel flow. Although the diamagnetic drift vector is perpendicular to the magnetic field, its geometric vertical component, like its [toroidal component](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), need not vanish. The species-level [ion velocity due to diamagnetic drift](name:ion_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of that species. Its vertical projection is therefore the density-weighted mean of the corresponding charge-state vertical components, not their sum. Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic fluid drift of the specified ion charge state has a component toward increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Particle number density of a selected plasma population evaluated at the plasma boundary, the last closed magnetic flux surface separating confined plasma from the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation: Particle number density at the plasma boundary is the amount of a selected particle population per physical volume at the boundary of magnetically confined plasma. The population is intentionally unspecified by this parent quantity and is fixed by each specialized instance. The defining zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_P(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\int f_P(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_P$ is the number density of population $P$, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_P$ is the velocity distribution function of population $P$, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The selected population may be an electron population, an ion or impurity population, a neutral population, an elemental population, or an effective isotope mixture. The aggregation convention is additive over exactly the particles included in population $P$; inclusion of neutral particles and summation over charge states are specialization-dependent and are not fixed by this subject-less parent quantity. This boundary quantity is distinct from [density_at_magnetic_axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis) and [density_at_limiter](name:density_at_limiter), which use different loci. Specialized instances fix the population and its aggregation convention: [electron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) selects electrons, while [krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary) selects krypton ions with charge-state aggregation. Elemental variants such as [boron_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:boron_density_at_plasma_boundary) may include both neutral atoms and ionic charge states. When population and aggregation are held fixed, the corresponding boundary value is the locus-specific counterpart of density evaluated at another defined plasma location.

items.name: back_surface_neutron_flux
items.description: Back-surface neutron flux is the scalar energy flux carried by fusion neutrons escaping through the back surface of an applicable component or module. It is aggregated over neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations; it is not a maximum over the surface.
items.documentation: Back-surface neutron flux is the scalar surface density of power carried by fusion neutrons crossing outward through the back surface of the applicable component or module. It characterizes the local neutron energy load at that rear surface, not a vector flux and not a surface aggregate. The local scalar flux $q_n$ at a point $\boldsymbol{r}$ on the back surface is defined by $$ q_n(\boldsymbol{r}) = \frac{dP_{n,\mathrm{out}}}{dA}(\boldsymbol{r}) $$ where $q_n$ is the back-surface neutron flux, $\boldsymbol{r}$ is a point on the back surface, $P_{n,\mathrm{out}}$ is the power carried by fusion neutrons crossing outward through that surface, and $A$ is area on the back surface. The scope is the back surface only: the surface opposite the front or plasma-facing side of the object under consideration. The quantity is aggregated over neutron energies, fusion reaction channels, and reacting populations unless a more specific standard name states a narrower selection. This quantity excludes neutron source strength in a volume, total neutron power integrated over an area, flux at other surfaces, and any extremum selected over the back surface. A surface aggregate such as [maximum back-surface neutron flux](name:maximum_of_back_surface_neutron_flux) is obtained by taking the maximum value of this quantity over the applicable back surface; the maximum operation is not part of `back_surface_neutron_flux` itself. The area integral of $q_n$ over a chosen part of the back surface gives the neutron power crossing outward through that part, while the local value remains the surface-density quantity defined at each point.

items.name: density_at_pedestal_maximum
items.description: Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density evaluated at the pedestal maximum, the steep mid-pedestal locus of maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. It is a density value at that locus, not a density gradient.
items.documentation: Density at pedestal maximum is the selected plasma-particle number density evaluated at the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal), the steep mid-pedestal locus of maximum pedestal-gradient magnitude. The word maximum identifies the peak-gradient pedestal locus, not a maximum of the density value itself. The defining relation is the evaluation of the selected density function at that flux-coordinate locus: $$ n_{\mathrm{ped,max}} = n(\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}) $$ where $n_{\mathrm{ped,max}}$ is the density at pedestal maximum, $n(\psi_N)$ is the selected plasma-particle number density as a function of the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\psi_N$, and $\psi_{N,\mathrm{ped}}$ is the [normalized poloidal-flux coordinate of the pedestal maximum](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). This parent quantity is species- or population-generic; concrete children, such as [electron density at pedestal maximum](name:electron_density_at_pedestal_maximum), specialize the selected particle population without changing the locus definition. When the selected population is a species with charge states, the species-level density is summed over all charge states unless a charge-state-resolved name explicitly identifies one charge state. It excludes pedestal-top density and any local slope or maximum-gradient magnitude with respect to $\psi_N$; those quantities are distinct from the density value evaluated at this locus.

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_real_part
items.description: Real part of the first-order radial magnetic-vector-potential eigenfunction for a single toroidal mode in the vacuum region.
items.documentation: The quantity is the real radial projection of the first-order perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region for one toroidal Fourier mode. The real part is defined relative to the phase reference of that complex eigenfunction. $$ A_{R,\mathrm{vac}}^{\mathrm{Re}} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left(\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right) $$ Here $A_{R,\mathrm{vac}}^{\mathrm{Re}}$ is the requested real radial component, $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the complex first-order perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region, $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector, and $\operatorname{Re}$ denotes the real-part operation. The radial direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity applies outside the plasma and to one toroidal Fourier mode; it is not summed over modes. It excludes the plasma-region perturbation, the imaginary component, and the unreduced complex radial component. The [radial perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) is the full complex parent quantity, of which this entry is the real-part component. It is distinct from the [radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field), which is a magnetic-field perturbation rather than a vector potential. Sign convention: Positive when the real radial projection points toward increasing major radius $R$.

items.name: line_averaged_total_ion_temperature
items.description: Density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, with all species and charge states contributing by number density and averaged along a specified plasma chord.
items.documentation: The line-averaged total ion temperature is the line average of the local density-weighted effective temperature of the combined thermal ion population, including all included thermal ion species and charge states. It represents random thermal motion and excludes directed bulk-flow energy. The chord average is defined by $$ T_{i,\mathrm{line}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{C}} T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)\,d\ell}{\int_{\mathcal{C}}d\ell} $$ where $T_{i,\mathrm{line}}$ is the line-averaged quantity, $T_{i,\mathrm{tot}}(\ell)$ is the local [total ion temperature](name:total_ion_temperature), $\ell$ is path length along the chord, and $\mathcal{C}$ is the specified chord. Species and charge states are combined by number density before the line average is taken.
