Unlike the [volume-averaged total ion temperature](name:volume_averaged_total_ion_temperature), this quantity weights positions by chord length rather than plasma volume.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_at_wall
items.description: Incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal quantum state as they arrive at a plasma-facing wall.
items.documentation: This quantity is the incident kinetic-energy flux density carried by neutral atoms or molecules in a specified internal quantum state as they cross onto a plasma-facing wall. It includes only translational kinetic energy and only particles moving from the plasma toward the wall. $$ q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w<0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\left(-\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w\right) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ Here $q_{\mathrm{kin},s}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ is the incident kinetic-energy flux density, $s$ identifies the internal quantum state, $m_s$ is the particle mass, $\mathbf{v}$ is velocity relative to the wall, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}_w$ is the unit normal directed from the wall toward the plasma, and $f_s(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of that state. Unlike [neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall](name:neutral_internal_state_particle_flux_at_wall), this quantity weights arrivals by translational kinetic energy; neutral_energy_flux_at_wall aggregates the corresponding kinetic-energy flux over internal states. Internal excitation, potential, and rest-mass energies are excluded.

items.name: radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Radial component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction for a linear MHD mode, retaining its signed projection toward increasing major radius.
items.documentation: Radial component of the first-order perturbed plasma magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction associated with a linear MHD mode. The radial component is defined by $$ \delta A_R = \delta\mathbf{A} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}} $$ where $\delta A_R$ is the radial component, $\delta\mathbf{A}$ is the perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. This quantity represents one signed component of the plasma perturbation about a reference state; it is not the complete vector, a magnitude, a sum, or an average. The complete vector quantity is the [perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential), while the [poloidal perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential) provides an adjacent directional component. It includes the full radial eigenfunction rather than selecting only its real or imaginary quadrature; the latter is represented by the [radial perturbed plasma magnetic vector potential imaginary part](name:radial_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part). The associated perturbed magnetic field $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is obtained from the curl relation $\delta\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\delta\mathbf{A}$, where $\delta\mathbf{B}$ is the perturbed magnetic field and $\nabla\times$ is the spatial curl operator. The vector potential is gage-dependent, whereas its curl determines the corresponding magnetic-field perturbation. Sign convention: Positive when $\delta A_R$ points toward increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: effective_thermal_ion_charge_state_energy_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Effective vector velocity for convective transport of thermal energy by ions in one specified charge state.
items.documentation: The thermal ion charge-state energy convection velocity is the effective vector advection velocity assigned to convective transport of thermal energy by ions in one specified charge state. It represents the convective channel rather than the full particle velocity or diffusive energy transport. For the selected charge state, it is defined through the convective thermal-energy flux: $$ \mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{th}}\,\mathbf{v}_{E,\mathrm{conv}} $$ where $\mathbf{q}_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the convective thermal-energy flux, $\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal-energy transport density used in the flux decomposition, and $\mathbf{v}_{E,\mathrm{conv}}$ is the effective convection velocity. No summation over ion charge states is implied. The quantity excludes diffusive and conductive energy transport and need not equal the mass-weighted [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity); its radial instance is represented by the [radial effective thermal ion charge-state energy convection velocity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_energy_convection_velocity). Sign convention: Positive when each vector component points along its positive basis direction—increasing $R$, increasing $\phi$, or increasing $Z$—in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_focal_length_of_beamlet_group
items.description: Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the distance along the neutral-beam line from the group’s ion source to the point where the group’s vertical extent is minimized.
items.documentation: Vertical focal length of a beamlet group is the path length along the neutral-beam line from the beamlet group's ion source to the group vertical focus. The group vertical focus is the location at which the collective beamlet envelope has its minimum vertical extent, with vertical measured parallel to $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Using an along-beam coordinate $s$ that increases from the ion source along the neutral-beam line, the focal length is defined by $$ f_v = s_f - s_0, \qquad w_v(s_f) = \min_s w_v(s) $$ where $f_v$ is the vertical focal length of the beamlet group, $s_0$ is the ion-source position on the along-beam coordinate, $s_f$ is the vertical-focus position, and $w_v(s)$ is the collective vertical envelope extent of the beamlet group at position $s$. The quantity applies to one beamlet group and aggregates all beamlets in that group through their collective vertical envelope. It is not a per-beamlet focal length and not a whole-unit focal length formed by combining multiple groups; the distance is along the beam-line path rather than a vertical separation. It is distinct from the source-surface vertical width of a beamlet group and from any vertical extent at locations other than the focus; those are transverse extents, whereas this quantity is the along-beam separation to the location of the minimum. It is the vertical counterpart of the horizontal focal length of a beamlet group, which uses the minimum horizontal extent instead of the minimum vertical extent.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_separatrix
items.description: Dimensionless toroidal-flux surface label at the magnetic separatrix, identifying the outermost closed magnetic surface and its outer normalization value.
items.documentation: This quantity is the normalized toroidal-flux surface label evaluated at the magnetic separatrix, which is the outermost closed magnetic surface. It identifies the flux-coordinate location of separatrix quantities rather than a cylindrical distance or a local vector component. The normalized toroidal-flux coordinate at the separatrix is defined by $$ \left.\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}\right|_{\mathrm{sep}} = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,sep}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2} $$ where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux coordinate, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,sep}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the separatrix, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,LCFS}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the last closed flux surface. The separatrix is the last closed flux surface for this evaluation, so the value is the outer normalization value, equal to one when the separatrix and last-closed-surface loci are identified. This is a point evaluation of a scalar magnetic-surface label for the separatrix locus; it is not a spatial average, volume integral, flux integral, cylindrical radius, or vector component. The [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate) represents the same coordinate on general nested magnetic surfaces, while this quantity fixes its evaluation at the separatrix. The normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the plasma boundary uses the plasma-boundary locus instead. Those loci may coincide when the plasma boundary is defined as the last closed flux surface, but the two quantities retain distinct locus semantics.

items.name: vertical_wave_electric_field
items.description: Complex phasor of an electromagnetic-wave electric field projected onto the vertical Z direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, preserving local amplitude and phase.
items.documentation: The vertical wave electric field is the complex phasor obtained by projecting the electromagnetic-wave electric-field phasor onto the vertical basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. It is the Z-directed component of the [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field), retaining its local amplitude and phase. The projection is defined by $$ \widetilde{E}_Z(\mathbf{r},\omega)=\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}(\mathbf{r},\omega)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{Z}} $$ where $\widetilde{E}_Z$ is the vertical wave-electric-field phasor, $\widetilde{\mathbf{E}}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the complex wave-electric-field vector phasor, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, $\omega$ is angular frequency, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the vertical unit vector. This wave contribution is distinct from the static [vertical electric field](name:vertical_electric_field) and from the field-aligned [parallel wave electric field](name:parallel_wave_electric_field). Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field phasor projection is along $+\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$, the direction of increasing vertical coordinate $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_beam_tracing_beam
items.description: Vertical Z coordinate of a beam-tracing beam position along its propagation path, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the vertical coordinate of a ray or beam position evaluated along the propagation path of a beam-tracing beam. It identifies the position's height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R}, \hat{\phi}, \hat{Z})$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coordinate is the projection of the beam position onto the vertical direction: $$ z = \mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{Z} $$ where $z$ is the vertical coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of the beam point, and $\hat{Z}$ is the vertical unit vector of the right-handed cylindrical frame. This quantity applies to each beam position along the propagation path and is not aggregated over path positions or over multiple rays or beams. It describes geometric location only; it is not a wave amplitude, magnetic or electric field component, or propagation-direction quantity. It is distinct from the [vertical coordinate of the launching position](name:vertical_coordinate_of_launching_position), which identifies the beam's physical launch point rather than a general position along the path. At the launch point, the two coordinates may have the same value.

items.name: perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description: Gage-dependent perturbation of the vacuum magnetic vector potential generated by external current sources; its curl gives the corresponding induction perturbation excluding plasma-current contributions.
items.documentation:
The perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential is a gage-dependent vector field representing the perturbation of the external-source contribution to the [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential) relative to a specified reference state. It is the complete vector perturbation, not a single directional component. The corresponding perturbed vacuum magnetic induction is defined by: $$ \delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}} = 
abla 	imes \delta \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} $$ where $\delta \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential, $\delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the magnetic-induction perturbation produced by external sources, and $
abla 	imes$ is the curl operator. The perturbation remains gage-dependent: replacing $\delta \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ by $\delta \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} + 
abla \chi$, where $\chi$ is a scalar gage function, leaves $\delta \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ unchanged. This quantity includes the aggregate perturbation of the external-source contribution and excludes magnetic-vector-potential contributions generated by plasma currents. It is distinct from the unperturbed [vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) and from the full magnetic vector potential that includes plasma-current contributions. Its radial projection is represented by the [radial perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), while the corresponding unperturbed radial component is the [radial vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential). Components are resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of the vector points along its corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: vertical_coordinate_of_annulus_center
items.description: Vertical coordinate of the annulus center specifies its signed height from the zero-height plane, parallel to the symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: Vertical coordinate of the annulus center is its signed height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The coordinate is defined by $$ Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}} $$ where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the annulus center measured from the coordinate origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector parallel to the symmetry axis toward increasing $Z$. The quantity applies to one annular cross-section, not to points along its boundary or to an average over multiple elements. It specifies position rather than the inner radius, outer radius, or vertical extent of the annulus, and applies to both conducting and magnetizable components. It uses the same vertical projection as the [vertical coordinate of an arc-of-circle center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_arc_of_circle_center), with a different geometric locus. Sign convention: Positive when the annulus center lies above the zero-height plane in the direction of increasing $Z$.

items.name: particle_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Effective advection velocity characterizing non-diffusive transport in the plasma particle channel by bulk convection, without selecting a species or internal state.
items.documentation: Particle convective velocity is the effective vector velocity associated with non-diffusive transport of plasma particles by bulk convection. It describes motion of the transported particle quantity rather than diffusive spreading or the particle flux itself. For the particle transport channel, the convective particle flux is defined by $$ \mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p = n_p\,\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p $$ where $\mathbf{\Gamma}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p$ is the convective particle flux, $n_p$ is the local particle number density, and $\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{conv}}_p$ is the particle convective velocity. The subscript $p$ identifies the particle transport channel, and the superscript $\mathrm{conv}$ identifies its non-diffusive convective contribution. This is the full vector, channel-level quantity with no selected radial, poloidal, toroidal, or field-parallel component. It applies generically to plasma-particle transport without selecting a particular species, charge state, or internal state; no additional species-level aggregation is implied by the generic channel name. It excludes diffusive transport and must not be interpreted as the single-particle kinematic velocity of an individual particle. The quantity is the particle-channel specialization of [velocity due to convection](name:velocity_due_to_convection). The corresponding [energy velocity due to convection](name:energy_velocity_due_to_convection) uses the same effective-velocity construction for convective energy transport, while [neutral state convection velocity](name:neutral_state_convection_velocity) is a narrower quantity restricted to a specified neutral internal state. The vector components are expressed in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Sign convention: Positive when a vector component points along the corresponding positive basis direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.
